title.raw: 卷一百〇三 載記第三 劉曜 Volume 103 Records 3: Liu Yao

sentences.zh: 劉曜

translations.literal: Liu Yao.
translations.idiomatic: Biographical entry: Liu Yao.

sentences.zh: 劉曜，字永明，元海之族子也。

translations.literal: Liu Yao, courtesy name Yongming, was a kinsman’s son of Yuanhai.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Yao, whose courtesy name was Yongming, was a clansman of Liu Yuan (Yuanhai).

sentences.zh: 少孤，見養於元海。

translations.literal: He lost his parents young and was reared by Yuanhai.
translations.idiomatic: Orphaned young, he was raised by Liu Yuan.

sentences.zh: 幼而聰彗，有奇度。

translations.literal: In childhood he was clever and quick and had unusual breadth.
translations.idiomatic: Even as a child he was quick-witted and possessed an uncommon breadth of mind.

sentences.zh: 年八歲，從元海獵於西山，遇雨，止樹下，迅雷震樹，旁人莫不顛仆，曜神色自若。

translations.literal: At age eight he followed Yuanhai hunting in the Western Hills; they met rain and stopped under a tree; a sudden thunderbolt shook the tree; those beside him all toppled, but Yao’s expression was as before.
translations.idiomatic: When he was eight he accompanied Liu Yuan on a hunt in the western hills; as rain forced them to shelter under a tree, a thunderbolt struck it, sending everyone else scrambling while Liu Yao remained perfectly composed.

sentences.zh: 元海異之曰：「此吾家千里駒也，從兄為不亡矣！

translations.literal: Yuanhai marvelled and said, “This is our family’s swift colt; the senior line is not perished!
translations.idiomatic: Liu Yuan exclaimed in wonder, “Here is the thousand-li steed of our clan—my kinsman’s line will not die out after all!

sentences.zh: 」身長九尺三寸，垂手過膝，生而眉白，目有赤光，須髯不過百餘根，而皆長五尺。

translations.literal: ” He was nine chi three cun in height; his hands hung past his knees; from birth his eyebrows were white, his eyes had a red gleam; his beard had not more than a hundred-odd hairs, yet each was five chi long.
translations.idiomatic: ” He stood nine feet three inches tall, with hands that reached below his knees; his eyebrows were white from birth and his eyes held a ruddy gleam; his beard counted fewer than a hundred hairs, yet each strand measured five feet.

sentences.zh: 性拓落高亮，與眾不群。

translations.literal: In nature he was expansive, lofty, and bright, not of a kind with the crowd.
translations.idiomatic: By temperament he was openhanded and high-minded, standing apart from ordinary men.

sentences.zh: 讀書志於廣覽，不精思章句，善屬文，工草隸。

translations.literal: In reading his ambition lay in broad perusal; he did not fine-grind chapter and sentence; he was skilled at composing texts and accomplished at cursive and clerical script.
translations.idiomatic: He read for wide learning rather than hairsplitting textual analysis; he wrote well and excelled at cursive and clerical calligraphy.

sentences.zh: 雄武過人，鐵厚一寸，射而洞之，于時號為神射。

translations.literal: His martial prowess surpassed others; iron an inch thick, he shot and pierced it; at the time he was called divine archer.
translations.idiomatic: His martial prowess was extraordinary: he could send an arrow through an inch of iron, and men called him the divine bowman of his day.

sentences.zh: 尤好兵書，略皆暗誦。

translations.literal: He especially loved military books and largely recited them from memory.
translations.idiomatic: He especially devoured military treatises until he knew them virtually by heart.

sentences.zh: 常輕侮吳、鄧，而自比樂毅、蕭、曹，時人莫之許也，惟聰每曰：「永明，世祖、魏武之流，何數公足道哉！」

translations.literal: He often slighted Wu and Deng and compared himself to Yue Yi, Xiao, and Cao; people of the time did not grant it; only Cong often said, “Yongming is of the kind of Shizu and Wei Wu—what do those several men amount to!”
translations.idiomatic: He habitually disparaged Wu Qi and Deng Yu while likening himself to Yue Yi, Xiao He, and Cao Cao—contemporaries dismissed the boast. Only Liu Cong would say, “Yongming belongs with Emperor Guangwu and Cao Cao; those others are not worth discussing.”

sentences.zh: 弱冠游於洛陽，坐事當誅，亡匿朝鮮，遇赦而歸。

translations.literal: At weak-crown he travelled in Luoyang; he sat in an affair warranting execution, fled and hid in Korea, met amnesty and returned.
translations.idiomatic: In his youth he sojourned in Luoyang; accused of a capital crime, he fled to Korea until an amnesty allowed him to come home.

sentences.zh: 自以形質異眾，恐不容於世，隱跡管涔山，以琴書為事。

translations.literal: He thought himself in form and substance different from the multitude and feared not to be accommodated in the world; he hid his tracks on Mount Guancen and took zither and books as his occupation.
translations.idiomatic: Believing his striking appearance would invite mistrust, he withdrew to Mount Guancen and devoted himself to music and books.

sentences.zh: 嘗夜閒居，有二童子入跪曰：「管涔王使小臣奉謁趙皇帝，獻劍一口。

translations.literal: Once at night resting leisurely, two child attendants entered, knelt, and said, “The prince of Guancen sends your servant to pay respects to the Zhao emperor and present one sword.
translations.idiomatic: One night, as he sat alone, two boys appeared, knelt, and said, “The lord of Mount Guancen sends us to greet the future emperor of Zhao and to offer this sword.

sentences.zh: 」置前再拜而去。

translations.literal: ” They placed it before him, bowed twice, and departed.
translations.idiomatic: ” They set the blade before him, bowed twice, and vanished.

sentences.zh: 以燭視之，劍長二尺，光澤非常，赤玉為室，背上有銘曰：「神劍禦，除眾毒。

translations.literal: By candle he examined it; the sword was two chi long, its lustre extraordinary; red jade formed the scabbard; on the back an inscription read, “Divine sword ward off, remove all poisons.
translations.idiomatic: By lamplight he saw a two-foot blade of unearthly sheen in a scabbard of red jade, inscribed with the words “divine blade to ward off every ill.

sentences.zh: 」曜遂服之。

translations.literal: ” Yao then wore it.
translations.idiomatic: ” Liu Yao henceforth wore it at his side.

sentences.zh: 劍隨四時而變為五色。

translations.literal: The sword with the four seasons changed into five colors.
translations.idiomatic: The sword shifted through five hues with the turning seasons.

sentences.zh: 元海世頻曆顯職，後拜相國，都督中外諸軍事，鎮長安。

translations.literal: In Yuanhai’s reign he repeatedly passed through eminent posts; later he was appointed Chancellor of State, area commander of all military within and without, and garrisoned Chang’an.
translations.idiomatic: Under Liu Yuan he rose through a series of high offices; he was later made chancellor of state, commander-in-chief of all armies within and without, and stationed at Chang’an.

sentences.zh: 靳准之難，自長安赴之。

translations.literal: At Jin Zhun’s disaster, from Chang’an he hastened to it.
translations.idiomatic: When Jin Zhun staged his coup, Liu Yao marched from Chang’an to answer the crisis.

sentences.zh: 至於赤壁，太保呼延晏等自平陽奔之，與太傅朱紀、太尉范隆等上尊號。

translations.literal: Arriving at Chibi, Grand Guardian Huyan Yan and others fled from Pingyang to him; with Grand Tutor Zhu Ji, Grand Commandant Fan Long, and others they elevated the honorific title.
translations.idiomatic: At Chibi he was joined by Grand Guardian Huyan Yan, who had fled Pingyang with others; together with Grand Tutor Zhu Ji, Grand Commandant Fan Long, and the rest they urged the imperial title upon him.

sentences.zh: 曜以僭即皇帝位，大赦境內，惟准一門不在赦例，改元光初。

translations.literal: Yao usurpingly ascended the emperor position, greatly amnestied within the borders; only Zhun’s one gate was not in the amnesty precedent; changed era to Guangchu.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Yao then took the throne in his own right, proclaimed a general amnesty that expressly excluded Jin Zhun’s clan, and adopted the reign title Guangchu.

sentences.zh: 以朱紀領司徒，呼延晏領司空，範隆以下悉復本位。

translations.literal: He made Zhu Ji head the Minister over the Masses, Huyan Yan head Minister of Works, Fan Long and below all restored original posts.
translations.idiomatic: He appointed Zhu Ji over the minister of education, Huyan Yan over public works, and returned Fan Long and subordinate officials to their former ranks.

sentences.zh: 使征北劉雅、鎮北劉策次於汾陰，與石勒為掎角之勢。

translations.literal: He ordered Conqueror-of-the-North Liu Ya and Pacifier-of-the-North Liu Ce to encamp at Fenyin, forming a pincer-hold situation with Shi Le.
translations.idiomatic: He stationed Liu Ya and Liu Ce at Fenyin, so that their forces and Shi Le’s hemmed Jin Zhun in from two sides.

sentences.zh: 靳准遣侍中卜泰降於勒，勒囚泰，送之曜。

translations.literal: Jin Zhun sent Palace Attendant Bu Tai to surrender to Le; Le imprisoned Tai and sent him to Yao.
translations.idiomatic: Jin Zhun sent Bu Tai to Shi Le to negotiate surrender; Shi Le held him captive and sent him on to Liu Yao.

sentences.zh: 謂泰曰：「先帝末年，實亂大倫，群閹撓政，誅滅忠良，誠是義士匡討之秋。

translations.literal: He said to Tai, “In the late emperor’s later years, truly the great human bonds were disordered; the eunuch hordes disturbed governance and extinguished loyal good men; truly it is the autumn for righteous men to rectify and punish.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Yao told him, “In the late emperor’s last years the proper moral order collapsed, eunuchs seized the government, and loyal ministers were slaughtered—the hour had come for men of honor to set things right.

sentences.zh: 司空執心忠烈，行伊霍之權，拯濟塗炭，使朕及此，勳高古人，德格天地。

translations.literal: The Minister of Works held a loyal and ardent heart, exercised the power of Yi and Huo, rescued and aided amid mire and charcoal, enabling Us to reach this; merit surpasses the ancients, virtue reaches heaven and earth.
translations.idiomatic: The minister of works acted with steadfast loyalty, wielded authority in the manner of Yi Yin and Huo Guang, and dragged the realm out of ruin so that we stand here today; his achievements tower over those of antiquity and his virtue reaches heaven and earth.

sentences.zh: 朕方寧濟大艱，終不以非命及君子賢人。

translations.literal: We are calming and crossing great hardship; ultimately We will not by wrongful fate reach gentlemen and worthy men.
translations.idiomatic: We mean to heal this great calamity and will never permit innocent death to befall the virtuous.

sentences.zh: 司空若執忠誠，早迎大駕者，政由靳氏，祭則寡人，以朕此意布之司空，宣之朝士。

translations.literal: If the Minister of Works holds sincerity and early welcomes the great chariot, governance proceeds by the Jin clan, sacrifices then the solitary person; let this Our meaning be spread to the Minister of Works, proclaimed to court officers.
translations.idiomatic: If he proves loyal and welcomes the court in good time, power may remain with the Jin house while ritual honors fall to us alone; convey this intent to him and to the officials.

sentences.zh: 」泰還平陽，具宣曜旨。

translations.literal: ” Tai returned to Pingyang and fully proclaimed Yao’s intent.
translations.idiomatic: ” Bu Tai returned to Pingyang and relayed Liu Yao’s message in full.

sentences.zh: 准自以殺曜母兄，沈吟未從。

translations.literal: Zhun himself because he had killed Yao’s mother and elder brother, hesitated and did not comply.
translations.idiomatic: Jin Zhun, having murdered Liu Yao’s mother and elder brother, hesitated and would not commit.

sentences.zh: 尋而喬泰、王騰、靳康、馬忠等殺准，推尚書令靳明為盟主，遣卜泰奉傳國六璽降於曜。

translations.literal: Soon Qiao Tai, Wang Teng, Jin Kang, Ma Zhong, and others killed Zhun, pushed Minister Director Jin Ming as covenant lord, sent Bu Tai bearing the six state succession seals to surrender to Yao.
translations.idiomatic: Soon Qiao Tai, Wang Teng, Jin Kang, Ma Zhong, and others slew Jin Zhun, raised Jin Ming as leader, and sent Bu Tai with the six imperial seals to submit to Liu Yao.

sentences.zh: 曜大悅，謂泰曰：「使朕獲此神璽而成帝王者，子也。

translations.literal: Yao was greatly pleased and said to Tai, “That enabled Us to obtain these divine seals and accomplish emperor-kingship is you.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Yao was overjoyed and told him, “You are the one through whom we gained these sacred seals and the throne.

sentences.zh: 」石勒聞之，怒甚，增兵攻之。

translations.literal: ” Shi Le heard it and was greatly angry; he increased troops to attack him.
translations.idiomatic: ” When Shi Le heard the news, he flew into a rage and poured more troops into the assault.

sentences.zh: 明戰累敗，遣使求救於曜，曜使劉雅、劉策等迎之。

translations.literal: Ming repeatedly lost in battle, sent envoys seeking rescue from Yao; Yao sent Liu Ya, Liu Ce, and others to welcome him.
translations.idiomatic: Jin Ming suffered repeated defeats and begged Liu Yao for aid; Liu Yao dispatched Liu Ya, Liu Ce, and others to escort him.

sentences.zh: 明率平陽士女萬五千歸於曜，曜命誅明，靳氏男女無少長皆殺之。

translations.literal: Ming led fifteen thousand Pingyang gentlemen and women to submit to Yao; Yao ordered Ming executed; Jin clan male and female without young or old were all killed.
translations.idiomatic: Jin Ming brought fifteen thousand civilians from Pingyang to Liu Yao, who had him executed and put every member of the Jin clan to the sword, young and old alike.

sentences.zh: 使劉雅迎母胡氏喪於平陽，還葬粟邑，墓號陽陵，偽諡宣明皇太后。

translations.literal: He sent Liu Ya to welcome Lady Hu’s remains from Pingyang, returned and buried at Suyi, tomb titled Yang Mausoleum, falsely posthumous titled Empress Dowager Xuanming.
translations.idiomatic: He sent Liu Ya to fetch his mother Lady Hu’s coffin from Pingyang for reburial at Suyi under the tomb name Yang Mausoleum, with the posthumous title Empress Dowager Xuanming.

sentences.zh: 僭尊高祖父亮為景皇帝，曾祖父廣為獻皇帝，祖防懿皇帝，考曰宣成皇帝。

translations.literal: He usurpingly honored great-great-grandfather Liang as Emperor Jing, great-grandfather Guang as Emperor Xian, grandfather Fang as Emperor Yi, father titled Emperor Xuancheng.
translations.idiomatic: He posthumously ennobled his great-great-grandfather Liang as Emperor Jing, his great-grandfather Guang as Emperor Xian, his grandfather Fang as Emperor Yi, and his father as Emperor Xuancheng.

sentences.zh: 徙都長安，起光世殿於前，紫光殿於後。

translations.literal: He shifted the capital to Chang’an, raised Guangshi Hall in front, Ziguang Hall behind.
translations.idiomatic: He moved the capital to Chang’an and erected the Guangshi Hall in front and the Ziguang Hall behind the palace.

sentences.zh: 立其妻羊氏為皇后，子熙為皇太子，封子襲為長樂王，闡太原王，沖淮南王，敞齊王，高魯王，徽楚王，征諸宗室皆進封郡王。

translations.literal: He established his wife Lady Yang as empress, son Xi as heir apparent, enfeoffed son Xí as Prince of Changle, Chan Prince of Taiyuan, Chong Prince of Huainan, Chang Prince of Qi, Gao Prince of Lu, Hui Prince of Chu; summoned various imperial clans all advanced to commandery prince.
translations.idiomatic: He enthroned his wife Lady Yang as empress, named his son Xi crown prince, enfeoffed his son Xí as Prince of Changle, Chan as Prince of Taiyuan, Chong as Prince of Huainan, Chang as Prince of Qi, Gao as Prince of Lu, and Hui as Prince of Chu, while promoting other imperial kinsmen to princely rank.

sentences.zh: 繕宗廟、社稷、南北郊。

translations.literal: He repaired ancestral temple, altars of soil and grain, south and north suburban altars.
translations.idiomatic: He restored the imperial ancestral temple, the altars of soil and grain, and the suburban sacrifice sites.

sentences.zh: 以水承晉金行，國號曰趙。

translations.literal: With water succeeding Jin’s metal line, the state title was called Zhao.
translations.idiomatic: Claiming the water phase to succeed the Jin’s metal, he named his dynasty Zhao.

sentences.zh: 牲牡尚黑，旗幟尚玄，冒頓配天，元海配上帝，大赦境內殊死已下。

translations.literal: Sacrificial victims esteemed black; banners esteemed dark red; Maodun paired with Heaven; Yuanhai paired with Supreme Lord; greatly amnestied within borders those below capital death.
translations.idiomatic: Sacrifices favored black victims, standards were dark; Modun was matched with Heaven and Liu Yuan with the Supreme God; a general amnesty swept the realm excepting capital crimes.

sentences.zh: 黃石屠各路松多起兵于新平、扶風，聚眾數千，附于南陽王保。

translations.literal: Huangshi butcher Lusong Duo raised troops in Xinping and Fufeng, gathered crowds several thousand, attached to Prince of Nanyang Bao.
translations.idiomatic: Lusong Duo, a Huangshi freeman, raised several thousand men in Xinping and Fufeng and threw in his lot with Sima Bao, the Prince of Nanyang.

sentences.zh: 保以其將楊曼為雍州刺史，王連為扶風太守，據陳倉；

translations.literal: Bao appointed his general Yang Man as Yongzhou inspector, Wang Lian as Fufeng grand warden, holding Chencang;
translations.idiomatic: Sima Bao made his general Yang Man inspector of Yongzhou and Wang Lian administrator of Fufeng, and they held Chencang;

sentences.zh: 張顗為新平太守，周庸為安定太守，據陰密。

translations.literal: Zhang Yi as Xinping grand warden, Zhou Yong as Anding grand warden, holding Yinmi.
translations.idiomatic: while Zhang Yi and Zhou Yong took Xinping and Anding and garrisoned Yinmi.

sentences.zh: 松多下草壁，秦隴氐羌多歸之。

translations.literal: Songduo descended to Caobi; Qin and Long Di and Qiang largely submitted to him.
translations.idiomatic: Lusong Duo moved down to Caobi, drawing many Di and Qiang clans from the Qin-Long region.

sentences.zh: 曜遣其軍騎劉雅、平西劉厚攻楊曼于陳倉，二旬不克。

translations.literal: Yao sent his army-rider Liu Ya, Pacifier-of-the-West Liu Hou to attack Yang Man at Chencang; twenty days did not overcome.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Yao sent Liu Ya and Liu Hou against Yang Man at Chencang, but after twenty days they still could not take the town.

sentences.zh: 曜率中外精銳以赴之，行次雍城，太史令弁廣明言於曜曰：「昨夜妖星犯月，師不宜行。

translations.literal: Yao led inner and outer picked keen to hasten there; marching halted at Yong city, Grand Astrologer Bian Guangming spoke to Yao saying, “Last night an evil star violated the moon; armies are not fit to move.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Yao led his best troops forward but stopped at Yongcheng when director of astronomy Bian Guangming warned, “An ill omen crossed the moon last night—the army should not march.

sentences.zh: 」乃止。

translations.literal: ” Then he stopped.
translations.idiomatic: ” He called the advance off.

sentences.zh: 敕劉雅等攝圍固壘，以待大軍。

translations.literal: He ordered Liu Ya and others to take over the siege and firm ramparts, awaiting the great army.
translations.idiomatic: He instructed Liu Ya to tighten the siege and fortify the camps until the main host arrived.

sentences.zh: 地震，長安尤甚。

translations.literal: Earth shook; Chang’an especially severe.
translations.idiomatic: The earth trembled, Chang’an worst of all.

sentences.zh: 時曜妻羊氏有殊寵，頗與政事，陰有餘之征也。

translations.literal: At the time Yao’s wife Lady Yang had exceptional favor, rather participated in government affairs; there was a sign of excess of yin.
translations.idiomatic: Lady Yang enjoyed extraordinary favor and meddled in statecraft—a dark omen of feminine dominance.

sentences.zh: 三年，曜發雍，攻陳倉，曼、連謀曰：「諜者適還，云其五牛旗建，多言胡主自來，其鋒恐不可當也。

translations.literal: Third year, Yao set out from Yong, attacked Chencang; Man and Lian plotted saying, “Spies just returned saying their five-ox banner is raised; many say the Hu ruler came in person; its edge perhaps cannot be withstood.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year Liu Yao marched from Yong against Chencang. Yang Man and Wang Lian conferred: scouts report the five-ox banner aloft and rumors that the Hu ruler leads in person—a foe we may not withstand.

sentences.zh: 吾糧廩既少，無以支久，若頓軍城下，圍人百日，不待兵刃而吾自滅，不如率見眾以一戰。

translations.literal: Our granaries are already few; there is no means to sustain long; if the army halts under the wall and besieges one hundred days, without waiting for weapons we extinguish ourselves; better lead the visible host in one battle.
translations.idiomatic: Our stores are low; we cannot endure a long siege. If we sit beneath the walls until starvation breaks us in a hundred days, we perish without a blow. Better meet them in open battle with every man we have.

sentences.zh: 如其勝也，關中不待檄而至；

translations.literal: If we are victorious, Guanzhong without awaiting proclamations will arrive;
translations.idiomatic: Win, and the passes will rally to us without a summons;

sentences.zh: 如其敗也，一等死，早晚無在。

translations.literal: if we are defeated, one kind of death, morning or evening no difference.”
translations.idiomatic: lose, and we die all the same—whether sooner or later makes little difference.”

sentences.zh: 」遂盡眾背城而陣，為曜所敗，王連死之，楊曼奔于南氐。

translations.literal: Then they used all the host with back to city and arrayed, were defeated by Yao; Wang Lian died in it; Yang Man fled to Southern Di.
translations.idiomatic: They drew up every man with their backs to the wall; Liu Yao broke them, killing Wang Lian while Yang Man fled to the southern Di.

sentences.zh: 曜進攻草壁，又陷之，松多奔隴城，進陷安定。

translations.literal: Yao advanced and attacked Caobi, again took it; Songduo fled to Long city; advanced and took Anding.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Yao took Caobi in turn; Lusong Duo bolted to Longcheng, and he pressed on to capture Anding.

sentences.zh: 保懼，遷于桑城。

translations.literal: Bao feared, moved to Sang city.
translations.idiomatic: Sima Bao, panic-stricken, withdrew to Sangcheng.

sentences.zh: 氐羌悉從之。

translations.literal: Di and Qiang all followed him.
translations.idiomatic: The Di and Qiang flocked after him.

sentences.zh: 曜振旅歸於長安，署劉雅為大司徒。

translations.literal: Yao shook troops and returned to Chang’an; appointed Liu Ya as Grand Minister over the Masses.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Yao marched back to Chang’an in triumph and named Liu Ya grand minister of education.

sentences.zh: 晉將李矩襲金墉，克之。

translations.literal: Jin general Li Ju raided Jinyong, overcame it.
translations.idiomatic: The Jin commander Li Ju surprised Jinyong and seized it.

sentences.zh: 曜左中郎將宋始、振威宋恕降于石勒。

translations.literal: Yao’s Left Gentleman of the Household Song Shi, Prestige-rousing Song Shu surrendered to Shi Le.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Yao’s officers Song Shi and Song Shu went over to Shi Le.

sentences.zh: 署其大將軍、廣平王嶽為征東大將軍，鎮洛陽。

translations.literal: He appointed his grand general, Prince of Guangping Yue as Conqueror-of-the-East Grand General, garrisoned Luoyang.
translations.idiomatic: He made his general Liu Yue, Prince of Guangping, east-conquering commander-in-chief and stationed him at Luoyang.

sentences.zh: 會三軍疫甚，嶽遂屯澠池。

translations.literal: Meeting the three armies plague severe, Yue then encamped Mianchi.
translations.idiomatic: When plague ravaged the army, Liu Yue pulled back to Mianchi.

sentences.zh: 石勒遣石生馳應宋始等，軍勢甚盛。

translations.literal: Shi Le sent Shi Sheng swiftly to respond to Song Shi and others; military momentum very strong.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Le rushed Shi Sheng to support Song Shi; the column grew formidable.

sentences.zh: 曜將尹安、趙慎等以洛陽降生，嶽乃班師，鎮於陝城。

translations.literal: Yao’s generals Yin An, Zhao Shen and others with Luoyang surrendered to Sheng; Yue then classed army, garrisoned Shancheng.
translations.idiomatic: Yin An, Zhao Shen, and other Liu Yao commanders handed Luoyang to Shi Sheng, so Liu Yue withdrew and encamped at Shancheng.

sentences.zh: 西明門內大樹風吹折，經一宿，樹撥變為人形，發長一尺，鬚眉長三寸，皆黃白色，有斂手之狀，亦有兩腳著裙之形，惟無目鼻，每夜有聲，十日而生柯條，遂成大樹，枝葉甚茂。

translations.literal: Inside Ximing Gate a great tree wind blew and broke; after one night, the uprooted tree changed into human form, hair one chi long, beard and eyebrows three cun long, all yellow-white; there was a folded-hands appearance, also two feet wearing skirt form; only no eyes and nose; each night there were sounds; ten days then grew twigs; thereupon became great tree, branches and leaves very lush.
translations.idiomatic: A great tree inside the Ximing Gate was snapped by wind; by morning the splintered trunk had twisted into a human shape—a foot of hair, three inches of whiskers, parchment pale, arms folded as if in obeisance, legs sketched like a skirt, yet no eyes or nose. Sounds came from it each night; within ten days it sprouted again into a flourishing tree.

sentences.zh: 長水校尉尹車謀反，潛結巴酋徐庫彭，曜乃誅車，囚庫彭等五十餘人于阿房，將殺之。

translations.literal: Colonel of Changshui Yin Che plotted rebellion, secretly allied Ba chief Xu Kupeng; Yao then executed Che, imprisoned Kupeng and fifty-plus others at Afang, about to kill them.
translations.idiomatic: Colonel of Changshui Yin Che plotted revolt with the Ba chieftain Xu Kupeng; Liu Yao executed Yin Che and jailed Kupeng and more than fifty followers at Epang, intending to put them to death.

sentences.zh: 光祿大夫遊子遠固諫，曜不從。

translations.literal: Grand Counsellor of the Household You Ziyuan firmly remonstrated; Yao did not follow.
translations.idiomatic: You Ziyuan, a senior adviser, pleaded in vain.

sentences.zh: 子遠叩頭流血，曜大怒，幽子遠而盡殺庫彭等，屍諸街巷之中十日，乃投之于水。

translations.literal: Ziyuan knocked head bleeding; Yao greatly angry, sequestered Ziyuan and killed all Kupeng and others, exposed corpses in streets and lanes ten days, then cast them in water.
translations.idiomatic: You Ziyuan battered his brow until it bled; Liu Yao, furious, threw him into prison, slaughtered Xu Kupeng’s party, left the corpses in the streets ten days, then cast them into the river.

sentences.zh: 於是巴氐盡叛，推巴歸善王句渠知為主，四山羌、氐、巴、羯應之者三十餘萬，關中大亂，城門晝閉。

translations.literal: Thereupon Ba Di all rebelled, raised Ba Guishan king Ju Zhiqu as lord; four-mountain Qiang, Di, Ba, Jie responding numbered three hundred thousand-plus; Guanzhong greatly disordered; city gates day closed.
translations.idiomatic: The Ba Di rose as one, acclaiming Ju Zhiqu, king of Guishan; more than three hundred thousand Qiang, Di, Ba, and Jie from the hills answered him. Guanzhong collapsed into chaos and the capital barred its gates even by day.

sentences.zh: 子遠又從獄表諫，曜怒甚，毀其表曰：「大荔奴不憂命在須臾，猶敢如此，嫌死晚邪？

translations.literal: Ziyuan again from prison submitted remonstrance; Yao very angry, tore his memorial saying, “Dali slave not worrying life in a moment, still dares so, think death late eh?
translations.idiomatic: From prison You Ziyuan sent another memorial; Liu Yao tore it up, shouting, “Slave of Dali, your life hangs by a thread and still you prate—is death too slow for you?

sentences.zh: 」叱左右速殺之。

translations.literal: ” He scolded left and right to quickly kill him.
translations.idiomatic: ” He barked at his guards to kill him at once.

sentences.zh: 劉雅、朱紀、呼延晏等諫曰：「子遠幽而尚諫者，所謂忠於社稷，不知死之將至。

translations.literal: Liu Ya, Zhu Ji, Huyan Yan and others remonstrated saying, “Ziyuan imprisoned yet still remonstrates is what is called loyal to altars and grain, not knowing death will arrive.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Ya, Zhu Ji, and Huyan Yan urged him, “Imprisoned yet still advising the throne—that is devotion to the state, heedless of his own end.

sentences.zh: 陛下縱弗能用，奈何殺之！

translations.literal: Your Majesty though cannot use, how kill him!”
translations.idiomatic: If you will not heed him, why murder him?”

sentences.zh: 若子遠朝誅，臣等亦暮死，以彰陛下過差之咎。

translations.literal: If Ziyuan morning executed, we ministers also evening die, to display Your Majesty’s fault of excess.”
translations.idiomatic: Execute him at dawn and you may as well execute us at dusk, laying your harshness bare to the world.”

sentences.zh: 天下之人皆當去陛下蹈西海而死耳，陛下復與誰居乎！

translations.literal: All under heaven’s people all ought leave Your Majesty tread West Sea and die; Your Majesty again with whom dwell!”
translations.idiomatic: The realm will cast you off to perish by the western sea; then whom will you rule?”

sentences.zh: 」曜意解，乃赦之。

translations.literal: ” Yao’s intention loosened; then pardoned him.
translations.idiomatic: ” Liu Yao relented and spared him.

sentences.zh: 於是敕內外戒嚴，將親討渠知。

translations.literal: Thereupon ordered inner and outer strict martial law, about to personally punish Zhiqu.
translations.idiomatic: He then proclaimed martial law throughout the court and prepared to lead the host against Ju Zhiqu himself.

sentences.zh: 子遠進曰：「陛下誠能納愚臣之計者，不勞大駕親動，一月之中可使清定。

translations.literal: Ziyuan advanced saying, “If Your Majesty truly can accept foolish minister’s plan, not toil great chariot personally move; within one month can make clear and settled.
translations.idiomatic: You Ziyuan urged, “Adopt this humble stratagem and your majesty need not ride to war; the region can be quiet within a month.

sentences.zh: 」曜曰：「卿試言之。

translations.literal: ” Yao said, “You try speak it.”
translations.idiomatic: ” Liu Yao said, “Speak.”

sentences.zh: 」子遠曰：「彼匪有大志，希竊非望也，但逼于陛下峻綱耳。

translations.literal: ” Ziyuan said, “They are not having great ambition, hoping to steal improper hope; only pressed by Your Majesty’s stern net.”
translations.idiomatic: ” You Ziyuan said, “They nurse no grand design; they rebelled only because your laws fell too heavily on them.”

sentences.zh: 今死者不可追，莫若赦諸逆人之家老弱沒奚官者，使迭相撫育，聽其復業，大赦與之更始。

translations.literal: Now dead cannot be pursued; better not equal amnesty various rebels’ families old weak consigned to eunuch offices, make mutually nurture, listen their restore livelihood, great amnesty with them renew beginning.
translations.idiomatic: The dead cannot return; better release the women, children, and aged condemned to the palace workhouses, let kin care for one another, allow them to resume their farms, and declare a general amnesty that truly begins anew.

sentences.zh: 彼生路既開，不降何待！

translations.literal: Their living road already opened, not submit what wait!”
translations.idiomatic: Give them a road back to life and they will kneel without further fighting.”

sentences.zh: 若渠知自以罪重不即下者，願假臣弱兵五千，以為陛下梟之，不敢勞陛下之將帥也。

translations.literal: If Zhiqu himself because guilt heavy not immediately submit, wish lend minister weak troops five thousand, to for Your Majesty decapitate him, not dare trouble Your Majesty’s generals.”
translations.idiomatic: If Ju Zhiqu still refuses out of pride, grant me five thousand light troops and I will deliver his head without troubling your captains.”

sentences.zh: 不爾者，今賊黨既眾，彌川被穀，雖以天威臨之，恐非年歲可除。

translations.literal: If not thus, now rebel party already many, fill valleys receive grain, though with celestial majesty overlook them, fear not years can remove.”
translations.idiomatic: Otherwise their numbers choke every valley and ripen grain for war; not even imperial majesty will root them out in one season.”

sentences.zh: 」曜大悅，以子遠為車騎大將軍、開府儀同三司、都督雍秦征討諸軍事。

translations.literal: ” Yao greatly pleased, made Ziyuan chariot-cavalry grand general, open office same as Three Offices, area commander Yong Qin campaign-punish all military affairs.
translations.idiomatic: ” Delighted, Liu Yao named You Ziyuan chariot-and-cavalry commander-in-chief with privy seal authority equal to the three dukes, and gave him overall command of the Yong-Qin campaigns.

sentences.zh: 大赦境內。

translations.literal: Greatly amnestied within borders.
translations.idiomatic: He proclaimed an empire-wide amnesty.

sentences.zh: 子遠次於雍城，降者十餘萬，進軍安定，氐羌悉下，惟句氏宗党五千餘家保存于陰密，進攻平之，遂振旅循隴右，陳安郊迎。

translations.literal: Ziyuan encamped at Yong city, submitters ten-plus myriad; advanced army An Ding, Di Qiang all descended; only Ju clan clique five thousand-plus households preserved at Yinmi; advanced attacked pacified it; then shook troops along Long right, Chen An suburb welcomed.
translations.idiomatic: You Ziyuan halted at Yongcheng; within days more than a hundred thousand surrendered. He marched on Anding, where the Di and Qiang submitted. Only five thousand Ju households held out at Yinmi until he stormed them flat. He then wheeled his columns through Longyou, met by Chen An with full ceremony at the border.

sentences.zh: 先是，上郡氐羌十餘萬落保險不降，酋大虛除權渠自號秦王。

translations.literal: Before this, Shang commandery Di Qiang ten-plus myriad settlements held defiles not submit; chief great Xuchu Quanqu self-titled King of Qin.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, well over a hundred thousand Di and Qiang households in Shang commandery had held the ravines and styled their leader Xuchu Quanqu king of Qin.

sentences.zh: 子遠進師至其壁下，權渠率眾來距，五戰敗之。

translations.literal: Ziyuan advanced army arrived at their rampart below; Quanqu led host came resist; five battles defeated him.
translations.idiomatic: You Ziyuan drove to their fortifications; Xuchu Quanqu sallied out five times and lost five times.

sentences.zh: 權渠恐，將降，其子伊余大言於眾曰：「往劉曜自來，猶無若我何，況此偏師而欲降之！

translations.literal: Quanqu feared, about to submit; his son Yiyu big speech to host saying, “Formerly Liu Yao came in person, still what could he do to me; how much more this partial army and wish to submit to it!
translations.idiomatic: Quanqu prepared to yield, but his son Yiyu harangued the men: “When Liu Yao came in person he could not break us—what can this scratch force demand of our surrender!

sentences.zh: 」率勁卒五萬，晨壓壘門。

translations.literal: ” He led picked soldiers fifty thousand, dawn pressed rampart gate.
translations.idiomatic: ” He led fifty thousand veterans to the glacis at dawn.

sentences.zh: 左右勸戰，子遠曰：「吾聞伊餘之勇，當今無敵，士馬之強，復非其匹；

translations.literal: Left and right urged battle; Ziyuan said, “I have heard Yiyu’s bravery, today none his match; soldiers and horses’ strength, again not his equal;
translations.idiomatic: His officers clamored to attack. You Ziyuan said, “Yiyu’s valor is unmatched and his host outnumbers ours;

sentences.zh: 又其父新敗，怒氣甚盛；

translations.literal: moreover his father newly defeated, angry qi very abundant;
translations.idiomatic: his father has just been humbled and burns for revenge;

sentences.zh: 且西戎剽勁，鋒銳不可擬也。

translations.literal: moreover western Rong swift-strength, edge keen cannot be compared.”
translations.idiomatic: western warriors strike like flame—our edge cannot meet theirs yet.”

sentences.zh: 不如緩之，使氣竭而擊之。

translations.literal: Better slow them, make qi exhaust then strike them.”
translations.idiomatic: Wait until their fury spends itself, then hit them.”

sentences.zh: 」乃堅壁不戰。

translations.literal: ” Then he held fast the walls and did not fight.
translations.idiomatic: ” He kept his men behind the walls and refused battle.

sentences.zh: 伊餘有驕色。

translations.literal: Yiyu had a proud expression.
translations.idiomatic: Yiyu wore a look of triumph.

sentences.zh: 子遠候其無備，夜，誓眾蓐食，晨，大風霧，子遠曰：「天贊我也！

translations.literal: Ziyuan waited until they were unprepared; at night he swore the host and took meal before dawn; at morning, great wind and fog; Ziyuan said, “Heaven assists Us!
translations.idiomatic: You Ziyuan watched for slack discipline; by night he roused the troops and had them eat before dawn. Morning brought wind and thick mist. “Heaven fights for us!” he cried.

sentences.zh: 」躬先士卒，掃壁而出，遲明覆之，生擒伊餘，悉俘其眾。

translations.literal: ” He personally led ahead the soldiers and men, swept the rampart and went out; near dawn he overwhelmed them, alive-captured Yiyu, wholly took prisoner their host.
translations.idiomatic: ” He led from the front, burst from the camp, and at first light overwhelmed them, taking Yiyu alive and rounding up his entire force.

sentences.zh: 權渠大懼，被髮割面而降。

translations.literal: Quanqu greatly feared, dishevelled hair and cut face and submitted.
translations.idiomatic: Terror-stricken, Xuchu Quanqu loosed his hair, gashed his face in submission, and yielded.

sentences.zh: 子遠啟曜以權渠為征西將軍、西戎公，分徙伊余兄弟及其部落二十餘萬口于長安。

translations.literal: Ziyuan opened to Yao making Quanqu Conqueror-of-the-West General, Duke of Western Rong, separately moved Yiyu’s brothers and their tribe more than two hundred thousand mouths to Chang’an.
translations.idiomatic: You Ziyuan memorialized to have Xuchu Quanqu named west-conquering general and duke of the western Rong, then resettled Yiyu, his brothers, and more than two hundred thousand tribespeople in Chang’an.

sentences.zh: 西戎之中，權渠部最強，皆稟其命而為寇暴，權渠既降，莫不歸附。

translations.literal: Among western Rong, Quanqu’s section was strongest; all received his orders and became bandit-violent; Quanqu having submitted, none did not attach.
translations.idiomatic: Of the western tribes Xuchu Quanqu’s band had been the strongest, raiding at his word; once he submitted, the rest came in without exception.

sentences.zh: 曜大悅，宴群臣於東堂，語及平生，泫然流涕，遂下書曰：「蓋褒德惟舊，聖-{后}-之所先；

translations.literal: Yao was greatly pleased, feasted the host of ministers in the eastern hall, spoke reaching his whole life, tearfully wept, then issued a document saying, “In general rewarding virtue and cherishing old ties is what sage rulers put first;
translations.idiomatic: Liu Yao was so pleased that he feasted his ministers in the eastern hall; as talk turned to his whole life he wept openly and then promulgated an edict: “To honor old virtue is the first duty of a wise sovereign;

sentences.zh: 念惠錄孤，明王之恆典。

translations.literal: remembering kindness and recording orphans is the constant canon of enlightened kings.
translations.idiomatic: to remember kindness and care for the orphaned is the standing rule of enlightened kings.

sentences.zh: 是以世祖草創河北，而致封于嚴尤之孫；

translations.literal: Therefore Shizu grass-founded Hebei, and thereupon enfeoffed the descendant of Yan You;
translations.idiomatic: Thus Emperor Guangwu, founding his rule north of the Yellow River, still enfeoffed a descendant of Yan You;

sentences.zh: 魏武勒兵梁宋，追慟於橋公之墓。

translations.literal: Wei Wu drilled troops in Liang and Song, pursued grief at Duke Qiao’s tomb.
translations.idiomatic: Cao Cao, the Wei Martial Emperor, campaigned through Liang and Song and mourned at the tomb of Duke Qiao.

sentences.zh: 前新贈大司徒、烈湣公崔岳，中書令曹恂，晉陽太守王忠，太子洗馬劉綏等，或識朕于童齔之中，或濟朕於艱窘之極，言念君子，實傷我心。

translations.literal: The lately posthumously gifted Grand Minister over the Masses, Duke Lie Min Cui Yue, Palace Secretary Cao Xun, Jinyang Administrator Wang Zhong, crown prince attendant Liu Sui, and others, either knew Us in the years of milk-teeth, or aided Us at the extreme of hardship and want; speaking of these gentlemen truly wounds Our heart.
translations.idiomatic: The late Cui Yue, posthumously grand minister of education and Duke Lie Min; Cao Xun, director of the secretariat; Wang Zhong, governor of Jinyang; Liu Sui, attendant to the heir apparent—some knew me as a child, others pulled me through utter destitution. To think of such men tears at my heart.

sentences.zh: 《詩》不云乎：『中心藏之，何日忘之！

translations.literal: Does not the “Poetry” say: “Hidden in the center, what day forget it!
translations.idiomatic: As the Classic of Poetry says, “Treasured in the heart—when could I forget?”

sentences.zh: 』岳，漢昌之初雖有褒贈，屬否運之際，禮章莫備，今可贈嶽使持節、侍中、大司徒、遼東公，恂大司空、南郡公，綏左光祿大夫、平昌公，忠鎮軍將軍、安平侯，並加散騎常侍。

translations.literal: ” Yue, at the beginning of Hanchang though there was praise-gift, belonging to the time of ill fortune’s juncture, ritual regulations were not complete; now can posthumously gift Yue bearer of credentials, palace attendant, grand minister over the masses, Duke of Liaodong, Xun grand minister of works, Duke of Nan commandery, Sui left grand master of golden seal, Duke of Pingchang, Zhong general who stabilizes the army, Marquis of Anping, and together add unattached cavalry attendant.
translations.idiomatic: ” Though Cui Yue was honored early in the Han-Chang era, the rites were never completed in that troubled time. Let him now receive posthumously the titles credential bearer, palace attendant, grand minister of education, and duke of Liaodong; Cao Xun, grand minister of works and duke of Nan commandery; Liu Sui, left grand master of golden seal and duke of Pingchang; Wang Zhong, general who stabilizes the army and marquis of Anping—each additionally as supernumerary cavalry attendant.

sentences.zh: 但皆丘墓夷滅，申哀莫由，有司其速班訪嶽等子孫，授以茅土，稱朕意焉。

translations.literal: But all mound-tombs are levelled and destroyed, extending grief has no means; responsible offices speedily promulgate inquiry for Yue and others’ descendants, invest them with fief soil, declaring Our intent.
translations.idiomatic: Yet their graves lie in ruins with no way to mourn them properly. Let officials quickly seek out the descendants of Cui Yue and the rest, invest them with fiefs, and so give voice to my gratitude.

sentences.zh: 」初，曜之亡，與曹恂奔于劉綏，綏匿之於舊匱，載送於忠，忠送之朝鮮。

translations.literal: ” At first, when Yao was a fugitive, he with Cao Xun fled to Liu Sui; Sui hid him in an old chest, cart-delivered to Zhong, Zhong sent him to Korea.
translations.idiomatic: ” In his flight Liu Yao had fled with Cao Xun to Liu Sui, who hid him in an old trunk, shipped him to Wang Zhong, and Wang Zhong sent him on to Korea.

sentences.zh: 歲餘，饑窘，變姓名，客為縣卒。

translations.literal: After more than a year, hunger and distress; he changed surname and name, lodged as a county runner.
translations.idiomatic: More than a year later, starving and desperate, he changed his name and hired himself out as a county runner.

sentences.zh: 嶽為朝鮮令，見而異之，推問所由。

translations.literal: Yue was Korea county magistrate, saw him and marvelled, pushed inquiry of the reason.
translations.idiomatic: Cui Yue was magistrate of that Korean county; struck by the man’s bearing, he pressed him until the story came out.

sentences.zh: 曜叩頭自首，流涕求哀。

translations.literal: Yao knocked head self-confessed, wept tears seeking pity.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Yao kowtowed, confessed all, and begged with tears.

sentences.zh: 嶽曰：「卿謂崔元嵩不如孫賓碩乎，何懼之甚也！

translations.literal: Yue said, “You think Cui Yuansong is not equal to Sun Binshuo—why so much fear!
translations.idiomatic: Cui Yue said, “Do you imagine Cui Yuansong less honorable than Sun Binshuo? Why such terror!

sentences.zh: 今詔捕卿甚峻，百姓間不可保也。

translations.literal: Now the edict seeking you is very severe; among common folk it cannot be guaranteed.
translations.idiomatic: The court’s warrant for you is ruthless; no common household can shield you.

sentences.zh: 此縣幽僻，勢能相濟，縱有大急，不過解印綬與卿俱去耳。

translations.literal: This county is remote; in situation able mutually to aid; even if great urgency, no more than stripping seal-ribbon and with you together going.
translations.idiomatic: This district is remote—we can help each other. At worst I surrender my seal and flee with you.

sentences.zh: 吾既門衰，無兄弟之累，身又薄祜，未有兒子，卿猶吾子弟也，勿為過憂。

translations.literal: We already gate-declined, no brothers’ burden; body again thin blessing, not yet having sons; you are still as Our sons and younger brothers; do not over-worry.
translations.idiomatic: My own house is in decline and I have no brothers to burden me; heaven has granted me no sons. You are family to me—do not torment yourself with fear.

sentences.zh: 大丈夫處身立世，鳥獸投人，要欲濟之，而況君子乎！

translations.literal: A great man placing body and establishing age, birds and beasts cast to men, desiring to save them—how much more gentlemen!
translations.idiomatic: A man who would make his way in the world aids even beasts that throw themselves on his mercy—how much more a fellow gentleman!

sentences.zh: 」給以衣服，資供書傳。

translations.literal: ” He supplied clothes and supplied books and commentaries.
translations.idiomatic: ” He gave Liu Yao clothing, books, and sustenance.

sentences.zh: 曜遂從嶽，質通疑滯，恩顧甚厚。

translations.literal: Yao then followed Yue, questioned through doubtful blockages, favor and regard very thick.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Yao stayed with Cui Yue, working through every doubt, and Cui Yue treated him with exceptional kindness.

sentences.zh: 岳從容謂曜曰：「劉生姿宇神調，命世之才也！

translations.literal: Yue calmly said to Yao, “Liu Sheng’s bearing and spirit-harmony, a fate-for-the-age’s talent!
translations.idiomatic: Cui Yue once said calmly, “This young Liu’s presence and spirit mark him as a man born to shape an age!

sentences.zh: 四海脫有微風搖之者，英雄之魁，卿其人矣。

translations.literal: Within the four seas if there be slight wind that shakes him, chief of heroes—you are that man.
translations.idiomatic: If ever the realm stirs, he will stand first among heroes—and you are he.

sentences.zh: 」曹恂雖於屯厄之中，事曜有君臣之禮，故皆德之。

translations.literal: ” Though Cao Xun was in the midst of hardship and obstruction, serving Yao had lord-minister ritual; therefore all prized them.
translations.idiomatic: ” Even when Cao Xun languished in adversity, he observed full court etiquette toward Liu Yao; both men earned lasting gratitude.

sentences.zh: 曜立太學于長樂宮東，小學于未央宮西，簡百姓年二十五已下十三已上，神志可教者千五百人，選朝賢宿儒明經篤學以教之。

translations.literal: Yao established the Grand Academy east of Changle Palace, the lesser school west of Weiyang Palace, selected commoners aged below twenty-five and above thirteen, spirit and mind teachable, one thousand five hundred persons, chose court worthies and hoary Confucians clear in classics and devoted in learning to teach them.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Yao founded an imperial academy east of Changle Palace and a primary school west of Weiyang, enrolling fifteen hundred common boys aged thirteen to twenty-five who showed aptitude, with veteran scholars of the classics appointed to instruct them.

sentences.zh: 以中書監劉均領國子祭酒。

translations.literal: He made Palace Supervisor Liu Jun head libationer of the imperial academy.
translations.idiomatic: He put Liu Jun, supervisor of the secretariat, in charge of the directorate of education.

sentences.zh: 置崇文祭酒，秩次國子。

translations.literal: He established exalted-text libationer, rank order following the imperial academy.
translations.idiomatic: He created the post of libationer for exalted letters, ranked just below the imperial academy.

sentences.zh: 散騎侍郎董景道以明經擢為崇文祭酒。

translations.literal: Gentleman consultant Dong Jingdao, by clarity in classics, was raised to exalted-text libationer.
translations.idiomatic: Dong Jingdao, a gentleman consultant distinguished for classical learning, was promoted to that new office.

sentences.zh: 以遊子遠為大司徒。

translations.literal: He made You Ziyuan grand minister over the masses.
translations.idiomatic: You Ziyuan was named grand minister of education.

sentences.zh: 曜命起酆明觀，立西宮，建陵霄台于滈池，又將於霸陵西南營壽陵。

translations.literal: Yao ordered raising Fengming Observatory, establishing Western Palace, building Lingxiao Terrace at Hao pool, and also about to at Bashiling southwest camp Shou Mausoleum.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Yao ordered the Fengming Observatory built, a western palace raised, the Lingxiao Terrace erected by the Hao River, and a lavish mausoleum planned southwest of Bashan.

sentences.zh: 侍中喬豫、和苞上疏諫曰：「臣聞人主之興作也，必仰准乾象，俯順人時，是以衛文承亂亡之後，宗廟社稷流漂無所，而猶上候營室以構楚宮。

translations.literal: Attendants Qiao Yu and He Bao submitted memorial remonstrating saying, “We have heard that when a human lord undertakes works, he must look up to align with celestial images, look down to comply with human seasons; therefore Duke Wen of Wei, inheriting after chaos and loss, ancestral temple and altars of soil and grain drifted and had nowhere, yet still upward waited Yingshi to construct Chu palace.
translations.idiomatic: Attendants Qiao Yu and He Bao memorialized: “A sovereign’s building projects must match heaven above and the season of men below. Even Duke Wen of Wey, after calamity had swept away temple and altars, still watched the Yingshi asterism before raising a palace at Chuqiu.

sentences.zh: 彼其急也猶尚若茲，故能興康叔、武公之跡，以延九百之慶也。

translations.literal: That they were urgent still was thus; therefore able to raise traces of Kang Shu and Duke Wu, to extend the nine-hundred years’ blessing.
translations.idiomatic: Though pressed to the limit, he acted with such care that the lines of Kang Shu and Duke Wu flourished and the house enjoyed nearly a thousand years of fortune.

sentences.zh: 奉詔書將營酆明觀，市道芻蕘咸以非之，曰一觀之功可以平涼州矣。

translations.literal: Receiving the edict document about to build Fengming Observatory, market-road hay-gatherers all by it deemed wrong, saying one observatory’s accomplishment could pacify Liangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: When your order went out to build the Fengming Observatory, folk in the markets cried waste, saying the cost of one tower could have pacified Liangzhou.

sentences.zh: 又奉敕旨復欲擬阿房而建西宮，模瓊台而起陵霄，此則費萬酆明，功億前役也。

translations.literal: Again receiving imperial order again wishing to model Epang and build Western Palace, copy Jade Terrace and raise Lingxiao—this then costs ten thousand Fengming, accomplishment hundred million former labor.
translations.idiomatic: New commands now copy Epang for a western palace and the Jade Terrace for Lingxiao—works that would dwarf the observatory ten thousandfold and outstrip every past levy.

sentences.zh: 以此功費，亦可以吞吳蜀，翦齊魏矣。

translations.literal: With this accomplishment expense, also could swallow Wu and Shu, clip Qi and Wei.
translations.idiomatic: For such sums you could conquer Wu and Shu and overrun Qi and Wei.

sentences.zh: 陛下何為于中興之日而蹤亡國之事！

translations.literal: Why does Your Majesty do in the day of restoration the deeds of a perished state!
translations.idiomatic: Why, at the very moment of revival, tread the path of fallen dynasties?

sentences.zh: 自古聖王，人誰無過！

translations.literal: From antiquity sage kings—who has had no fault!
translations.idiomatic: Even sage kings of old were not without error.

sentences.zh: 陛下此役，實為過舉。

translations.literal: Your Majesty’s this labor, truly is a fault-act.
translations.idiomatic: This campaign of yours is plainly a misstep.

sentences.zh: 過貴在能改，終之實難。

translations.literal: Fault values in able to change; carrying it to the end is truly hard.
translations.idiomatic: The mark of virtue is to mend a fault; persisting to the bitter end is the hard part.

sentences.zh: 又伏聞敕旨將營建壽陵，周回四里，下深二十五丈，以銅為棺郭，黃金飾之，恐此功費非國內所能辦也。

translations.literal: Moreover we humbly hear the imperial order will build Shou Mausoleum, circuit four li, below deep twenty-five zhang, using copper as outer coffin, yellow gold adorning it; we fear this accomplishment expense is not what within the state can accomplish.
translations.idiomatic: We also hear you mean to dig a tomb four li around and twenty-five zhang deep, sheathe the coffin in copper and plate it with gold—expenses the realm simply cannot bear.

sentences.zh: 且臣聞堯葬谷林，市不改肆；

translations.literal: Moreover we have heard Yao was buried in Gu Lin, market did not change stalls;
translations.idiomatic: Yao of antiquity slept in Gu Forest without disturbing the market stalls;

sentences.zh: 顓頊葬廣陽，下不及泉。

translations.literal: Zhuanxu was buried in Guangyang, below did not reach springs.
translations.idiomatic: Zhuanxu lay in Guangyang with earth barely covering him.

sentences.zh: 聖王之於終也如是。

translations.literal: Sage kings’ regarding the end is like this.
translations.idiomatic: Such was how sage kings treated death.

sentences.zh: 秦皇下錮三泉，周輪七里，身亡之後，毀不旋踵，暗主之於終也如此。

translations.literal: Qin Huang below fixed three springs, week wheel seven li; after body perished, destruction not turning heel; dark lords’ regarding the end is like this.
translations.idiomatic: The First Emperor of Qin sank shafts to the three subterranean streams and ringed seven li of mound; no sooner was he dead than the tomb was smashed. Thus foolish rulers end.

sentences.zh: 向魋石槨，孔子以為不如速朽；

translations.literal: Xiang Tui stone outer coffin, Confucius thought not equal to speedy rot;
translations.idiomatic: Confucius preferred swift decay to the stone sarcophagus of Xiang Tui;

sentences.zh: 王孫倮葬，識者嘉其矯世。

translations.literal: Wangsun Luo burial, knowing persons praised his correcting the age.
translations.idiomatic: Thoughtful men praised Wangsun Luo’s austere funeral for rebuking the vanity of the age.

sentences.zh: 自古無有不亡之國，不掘之墓，故聖王知厚葬之招害也，故不為之。

translations.literal: From antiquity there has been no state that does not perish, no tomb that is not dug; therefore sage kings know thick burial invites harm; therefore do not do it.
translations.idiomatic: No realm lasts forever; no tomb escapes the spade. Sage kings knew opulent burials invite robbery and refused them.

sentences.zh: 臣子之于君父，陵墓豈不欲高廣如山嶽哉！

translations.literal: As to ministers and sons toward lord and father, on tombs how not wish high and broad as mountains!
translations.idiomatic: Subjects wish their sovereign’s mound as grand as a mountain—

sentences.zh: 但以保全始終，安固萬世為優耳。

translations.literal: But take preserving whole beginning and end, securing firm ten thousand generations as superior.
translations.idiomatic: yet true filial piety means keeping the remains safe for ages to come.

sentences.zh: 興亡奢儉，冏然於前，惟陛下覽之。

translations.literal: Rise and fall, extravagance and thrift, shine plainly before; only may Your Majesty survey it.
translations.idiomatic: Splendor and ruin stand plain in history; we beg you to weigh them.”

sentences.zh: 」曜大悅，下書曰：「二侍中懇懇有古人之風烈矣，可謂社稷之臣也。

translations.literal: ” Yao was greatly pleased, issued document saying, “The two attendants earnestly earnest have ancient men’s wind and fierceness; can be called altars-and-grain ministers.
translations.idiomatic: ” Liu Yao was delighted and replied: “You two speak with the blunt courage of antiquity—you are true servants of the altars of soil and grain.

sentences.zh: 非二君，朕安聞此言乎！

translations.literal: If not the two lords, how would We hear these words!
translations.idiomatic: Without you I would never have heard such counsel!

sentences.zh: 以孝明於承平之世，四海無虞之日，尚納鐘離一言而罷北宮之役，況朕之暗眇，當今極弊，而可不敬從明誨乎！

translations.literal: With filial brightness in the age of inheritance peace, within the four seas without worry days, still accepted Zhong Li one word and stopped Northern Palace labor; how much more Our dim-slight, present utmost decay, and can not respect-follow bright instruction!
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xiaoming in a time of peace once heeded a single remonstrance from Zhong Li and halted the Northern Palace works; shall I, dull and ruling in extremity, refuse wise advice?

sentences.zh: 今敕悉停壽陵制度，一遵霸陵之法。

translations.literal: Now order wholly stop Shou Mausoleum system, wholly follow Baling’s method.
translations.idiomatic: I hereby scrap the planned mausoleum and adopt the frugal model of Emperor Wen’s tomb at Bashan.

sentences.zh: 《詩》不云乎：『無言不酬，無德不報。

translations.literal: Does not the “Poetry” say: “No word without answer, no virtue without recompense.
translations.idiomatic: The Poetry says, “No gift goes unanswered, no kindness unrewarded.”

sentences.zh: 』其封豫安昌子，苞平輿子，並領諫議大夫。

translations.literal: ” Enfeoff Yu as Anchangzi, Bao as Pingyuzi, together leading remonstrance grandee.
translations.idiomatic: ” I enfeoff Qiao Yu as viscount of Anchang and He Bao as viscount of Pingyu, both with the title grandee of remonstrance.

sentences.zh: 可敷告天下，使知區區之朝思聞過也。

translations.literal: Can spread announce the realm, causing to know this humble court’s thinking to hear fault.
translations.idiomatic: Let the empire be told that this court hungers for reproof.

sentences.zh: 自今政法有不便於時，不利社稷者，其詣闕極言，勿有所諱。

translations.literal: From now policy laws having what is not convenient to the times, not benefiting altars and grain, let them go to the gate and speak utmost, do not have what is concealed.
translations.idiomatic: Henceforth any policy harmful to the times or the state must be brought straight to the throne without reserve.”

sentences.zh: 」省酆水囿以與貧戶。

translations.literal: ” He reduced Feng water park to give to poor households.
translations.idiomatic: He also turned the imperial park by the Feng River over to the poor.

sentences.zh: 終南山崩，長安人劉終於崩所得白玉方一尺，有文字曰：「皇亡，皇亡，敗趙昌。

translations.literal: Zhongnan Mountain collapsed; Chang’an man Liu Zhong at the collapse obtained white jade one chi square, having written text saying, “Huang wang, huang wang, defeat Zhao chang.
translations.idiomatic: Mount Zhongnan gave way, and a Chang’an commoner named Liu Zhong picked from the rubble a foot-square white tablet inscribed, “The throne falls, the throne falls; Zhao’s glory ends.

sentences.zh: 井水竭，構五梁，咢酉小衰困囂喪。

translations.literal: Well water dries, frame five beams; E-you small wane, Kun Dun decline, Xiao perish.
translations.idiomatic: The well runs dry, the five rafters rise; in the E-you year power wanes, in the Kun-dun cycle the state withers, and clamor ends in mourning.”

sentences.zh: 嗚呼！

translations.literal: Alas!
translations.idiomatic: Alas!

sentences.zh: 嗚呼！

translations.literal: Alas!
translations.idiomatic: Alas again!

sentences.zh: 赤牛奮靷其盡乎！

translations.literal: Red ox strains the yoke—is this the end!
translations.idiomatic: The red ox strains at the traces—has the end come?”

sentences.zh: 」時群臣咸賀，以為勒滅之征。

translations.literal: ” At the time the host of ministers all congratulated, deeming it an omen of Le’s destruction.
translations.idiomatic: ” Courtiers hailed it as a sign that Shi Le would be destroyed.

sentences.zh: 曜大悅，齋七日而後受之於太廟，大赦境內，以終為奉瑞大夫。

translations.literal: Yao was greatly pleased, fasted seven days then afterward received it in the Grand Temple, greatly amnestied within the borders, making Zhong minister who presents auspicious.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Yao fasted seven days, installed the stone in the ancestral temple, proclaimed an amnesty, and named Liu Zhong bearer of auspicious portents.

sentences.zh: 中書監劉均進曰：「臣聞國主山川，故山崩川竭，君為之不舉。

translations.literal: Palace Supervisor Liu Jun advanced saying, “We have heard the state lord mountains and rivers; therefore mountain collapse river dry, the lord for it does not raise.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Jun, supervisor of the secretariat, objected: “The mountains and rivers embody the state; when they fail, the ruler suspends music and feasting.

sentences.zh: 終南，京師之鎮，國之所瞻，無故而崩，其凶焉可極言！

translations.literal: Zhongnan, the capital’s bulwark, what the state gazes on; without reason collapsing—its ill omen how can be fully spoken!
translations.idiomatic: Zhongnan is the buttress of the capital; for it to crumble without cause is calamity beyond words.

sentences.zh: 昔三代之季，其災也如是。

translations.literal: Formerly the three dynasties’ end-times, their disasters were like this.
translations.idiomatic: The last days of the three ancient dynasties looked just like this.

sentences.zh: 今朝臣皆言祥瑞，臣獨言非，誠上忤聖旨，下違眾議，然臣不達大理，竊所未同。

translations.literal: Now court ministers all speak auspicious omens; your servant alone speaks not, truly above offending holy edict, below violating host opinion; yet your servant not comprehending great pattern, privately not same.
translations.idiomatic: Today everyone cries auspice; I alone cry warning—defying your majesty and my colleagues alike, yet I cannot agree with them.

sentences.zh: 何則？

translations.literal: Why so?
translations.idiomatic: Why?

sentences.zh: 玉之于山石也，猶君之於臣下。

translations.literal: Jade’s relation to mountain stone is like lord’s relation to ministers below.
translations.idiomatic: Jade cleaves from the mountain as the sovereign stands above his ministers.

sentences.zh: 山崩石壞，象國傾人亂。

translations.literal: Mountain collapses stone breaks, image state overturns people in chaos.
translations.idiomatic: When peak and boulder shatter, it images a realm overturned and people in turmoil.

sentences.zh: 『皇亡，皇亡，敗趙昌者』，此言皇室將為趙所敗，趙因之而昌。

translations.literal: “Huang wang, huang wang, defeat Zhao chang”—this speech means the imperial house will be by Zhao defeated, Zhao thereby will flourish.
translations.idiomatic: The lines “The throne falls… Zhao’s glory ends” mean the ruling house will fall so that Zhao may rise.

sentences.zh: 今大趙都于秦雍，而勒跨全趙之地，趙昌之應，當在石勒，不在我也。

translations.literal: Now great Zhao is capitalled at Qin and Yong, while Le strides the whole Zhao region; Zhao flourish’s response ought to be at Shi Le, not at Us.
translations.idiomatic: Our “great Zhao” rules from Qin and Yong, but Shi Le holds the heartland of Zhao; the omen of Zhao’s rise points to him, not to us.

sentences.zh: 『井水竭，構五梁』者，井謂東井，秦之分也，『五謂五車』，梁謂大梁，五車、大梁，趙之分也，此言秦將竭滅，以構成趙也。

translations.literal: “Well water dries, frame five beams”—well means Eastern Well, Qin’s division; “five means Five Chariots”; Liang means Great Liang; Five Chariots, Great Liang, Zhao’s division; this speech means Qin will dry-exhaust, thereby constituting Zhao.
translations.idiomatic: “The well runs dry, the five rafters rise” alludes to the asterism Eastern Well, the celestial seat of Qin, and to the Five Chariots and Great Liang, which belong to Zhao’s sky chart—it foretells Qin’s exhaustion and Zhao’s triumph.

sentences.zh: 『咢』者，歲之次名作咢也，言歲馭作咢酉之年，當有敗軍殺將之事。

translations.literal: “E” refers to the year-branch name called E; it says the year when the cycle rides to E-you there will be defeated army slain general matters.
translations.idiomatic: The character “E” marks a calendrical phase; in the E-you year armies will be broken and generals slain.

sentences.zh: 『困』謂困敦，歲在子之年名，玄囂亦在天之次，言歲馭于子，國當喪亡。

translations.literal: “Kun” means Kun-dun, the year-name in zi; Xuan Xiao also is in heaven’s order; it says the year rides to zi, the state ought to perish.
translations.idiomatic: “Kun” names the kui-dun year of the rat; Xuan Xiao likewise sits in the sky’s sequence; when the cycle comes to zi the state faces ruin.

sentences.zh: 『赤牛奮靷』謂赤奮若，在醜之歲名也。

translations.literal: “Red ox strains yoke” means red fen-ruo, the year-name in chou.
translations.idiomatic: “The red ox strains” points to the chi-fen-ruo year of the ox.

sentences.zh: 『牛』謂牽牛，東北維之宿，醜之分也，言歲在醜當滅亡，盡無復遺也。

translations.literal: “Ox” means Ox-Herder, the lodging of northeast corner, chou’s division; it says year in chou ought to perish-exhaust, none again remaining.
translations.idiomatic: “Ox” is the Herd asterism in the northeast, the chou quarter; in the chou year nothing will survive.

sentences.zh: 此其誡悟蒸蒸，欲陛下勤修德化以禳之。

translations.literal: This its warning understanding steaming, desires Your Majesty diligently cultivate virtue and transformation to expel it.
translations.idiomatic: The inscription is a steaming, urgent warning: you must redouble virtuous rule to avert it.

sentences.zh: 縱為嘉祥，尚願陛下夕惕以答之。

translations.literal: Even if it be auspicious omen, still wish Your Majesty evening-fear to answer it.
translations.idiomatic: Even read as a blessing, you should stay wakeful nights and answer heaven with care.

sentences.zh: 《書》曰：『雖休勿休。

translations.literal: The “Document” says: “Though favorable, do not treat as favorable.
translations.idiomatic: The Documents says, “Though the signs seem fair, do not trust them as fair.”

sentences.zh: 』願陛下追蹤周旦盟津之美，捐鄙虢公夢廟之凶，謹歸沐浴以待妖言之誅。

translations.literal: ” Wish Your Majesty trace Zhou and Dan’s Mengjin beauty, cast aside vulgar Duke of Guo’s dream-temple ill, respectfully return bathe and wash awaiting inauspicious speech’s execution.
translations.idiomatic: ” I beg you to recall the virtue of the Duke of Zhou at Mengjin, spurn the ill omen of Duke Guo’s dream, bathe and purify yourself, and await punishment if my words prove false.”

sentences.zh: 」曜憮然改容。

translations.literal: ” Yao somberly changed expression.
translations.idiomatic: ” Liu Yao’s face fell.

sentences.zh: 御史劾均狂言瞽說，誣罔祥瑞，請依大不敬論。

translations.literal: The censor impeached Jun wild speech blind saying, deceiving and obscuring auspicious omens, requesting according to great irreverence judge.
translations.idiomatic: The imperial secretary indicted Liu Jun for mad slander that traduced a good omen and asked that he die for gross disrespect.

sentences.zh: 曜曰：「此之災瑞，誠不可知，深戒朕之不德，朕收其忠惠多矣，何罪之有乎！」

translations.literal: Yao said, “This’s disaster-auspice, truly cannot be known; deeply warning Our lack of virtue; We have received his loyal kindness much—what crime is there!”
translations.idiomatic: Liu Yao replied, “Whether this stone bodes good or ill we cannot know; it surely rebukes my want of virtue. I have already gained more than enough from his honesty—how could he be guilty?”

sentences.zh: 曜親征氐羌，仇池楊難敵率眾來距，前鋒擊敗之，難敵退保仇池，仇池諸氐羌多降於曜。

translations.literal: Yao personally campaigned Di and Qiang; Chouci Yang Nan-di led host came resist; vanguard defeated him; Nan-di retreated guarding Chouci; Chouci various Di and Qiang largely submitted to Yao.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Yao led a punitive expedition against the Di and Qiang. Yang Nan-di of Chouci marched to meet him but was routed by the van; he fell back on Chouci while most local Di and Qiang clans submitted to Liu Yao.

sentences.zh: 曜後復西討楊韜于南安，韜懼，與隴西太守梁勳等降於曜，皆封列侯。

translations.literal: Yao afterward again west campaigned Yang Tao at Nan’an; Tao feared, with Longxi Administrator Liang Xun and others submitted to Yao, all enfeoffed column marquises.
translations.idiomatic: Later Liu Yao struck west at Yang Tao in Nan’an. Yang Tao, terrified, surrendered with Liang Xun, administrator of Longxi, and others; all were enfeoffed as full marquises.

sentences.zh: 使侍中喬豫率甲士五千，遷韜等及隴右萬餘戶于長安。

translations.literal: He ordered Attendant Qiao Yu to lead armored soldiers five thousand, move Tao and others and Long right more than ten thousand households to Chang’an.
translations.idiomatic: He sent Qiao Yu with five thousand armored troops to relocate Yang Tao and more than ten thousand Longyou households to Chang’an.

sentences.zh: 曜又進攻仇池。

translations.literal: Yao again advanced attacking Chouci.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Yao pressed the attack on Chouci.

sentences.zh: 時曜寢疾，兼癘疫甚，議欲班師，恐難敵躡其後，乃以其尚書郎王獷為光國中郎將，使于仇池，以說難敵，難敵於是遣使稱籓。

translations.literal: At the time Yao bed-illness, together plague-epidemic very severe, deliberated wishing to recall army, feared Nan-di tread his rear, then made his secretary Wang Kuang light-country middle general, sent to Chouci, to persuade Nan-di; Nan-di thereupon sent envoy declaring vassalage.
translations.idiomatic: By then Liu Yao lay gravely ill while pestilence raged; his council urged retreat, yet he feared Yang Nan-di would strike his rear. He therefore named Wang Kuang, a secretary, middle general of the Radiant State and sent him to negotiate; Yang Nan-di then offered submission as a vassal.

sentences.zh: 曜大悅，署難敵為使持節、侍中、假黃鉞、都督益甯南秦涼梁巴六州隴上西域諸軍事、上大將軍、益甯南秦三州牧、領護南氐校尉、甯羌中郎將、武都王，子弟為公侯列將二千石者十五人。

translations.literal: Yao was greatly pleased, appointed Nan-di bearer of credentials, palace attendant, false yellow axe, area commander Yi Ning South Qin Liang Ba six states Long upland Western Regions all military affairs, supreme grand general, Yi Ning South Qin three prefectures shepherd, concurrently protector south Di colonel, Ningqiang middle general, Prince of Wudu, sons and younger brothers as marquises column generals two-thousand-dan fifteen persons.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Yao joyfully invested him with the yellow battle-axe, credentials, and palace rank, made him commander-in-chief over Yi, Ning, southern Qin, Liang, Ba, and the Long marches plus the Western Regions, supreme grand general, shepherd of three prefectures, protector-colonel of the southern Di, middle general of the Pacified Qiang, and prince of Wudu, while fifteen of his kinsmen received marquisates or colonelcies at the two-thousand-dan level.

sentences.zh: 陳安請朝，曜以疾篤不許。

translations.literal: Chen An requested court audience; Yao because illness severe did not permit.
translations.idiomatic: Chen An asked leave to visit the court; Liu Yao, deathly ill, refused.

sentences.zh: 安怒，且以曜為死也，遂大掠而歸。

translations.literal: An angry, and taking Yao as dead, thereupon greatly plundered and returned.
translations.idiomatic: Chen An took offense, assumed Liu Yao was already dead, and marched home in a frenzy of looting.

sentences.zh: 曜疾甚篤，馬輿而還，使其將呼延實監輜重於後。

translations.literal: Yao’s illness very severe, by horse-litter returned, ordered his general Huyan Shi to supervise baggage train in the rear.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Yao was too ill to ride and was carried back in a litter, leaving General Huyan Shi to guard the baggage train.

sentences.zh: 陳安率精騎耍之於道。

translations.literal: Chen An led picked cavalry waylaid them on the road.
translations.idiomatic: Chen An intercepted him with picked horsemen along the route.

sentences.zh: 實奔戰無路，與長史魯憑俱沒于安。

translations.literal: Shi ran, battle had no road, together with chief clerk Lu Ping both perished in An’s hands.
translations.idiomatic: Huyan Shi found every path blocked; he and his chief clerk Lu Ping fell into Chen An’s hands and died.

sentences.zh: 安囚實而謂之曰：「劉曜已死，子誰輔哉？

translations.literal: An imprisoned Shi and said to him, “Liu Yao is already dead—whom do you serve?
translations.idiomatic: Chen An threw him in chains and sneered, “Liu Yao is dead—who is left for you to serve?

sentences.zh: 孤當輿足下終定大業。

translations.literal: The solitary one ought with you, sir, finally settle the great enterprise.
translations.idiomatic: Stand with me and we will finish the great work together.

sentences.zh: 」實叱安曰：「狗輩！

translations.literal: ” Shi scolded An saying, “Dog pack!
translations.idiomatic: ” Huyan Shi roared back, “Cur!

sentences.zh: 汝荷人榮寵，處不疑之地，前背司馬保，今復如此。

translations.literal: You bore men’s glory and favor, dwelt in a place beyond doubt; before you betrayed Sima Bao, now again thus.
translations.idiomatic: You basked in imperial favor and faced no suspicion; first you turned on Sima Bao, and now you repeat the treason.

sentences.zh: 汝自視何如主上？

translations.literal: You yourself regard how compared to the lord above?
translations.idiomatic: How do you measure against our sovereign?

sentences.zh: 憂汝不久梟首上邽通衢，何謂大業！

translations.literal: We fear you not long will have head displayed at crossroads of Shanggui—what speak of great enterprise!
translations.idiomatic: Soon your skull will spike the highway at Shanggui—what “great work” is yours?

sentences.zh: 可速殺我，懸我首於上邽東門，觀大軍之入城也。

translations.literal: Can speed kill me, suspend my head at Shanggui east gate, watch the great army’s entering the city.
translations.idiomatic: Kill me now, nail my head to the east gate of Shanggui, and watch your city fall to the imperial host.

sentences.zh: 」安怒，遂殺之。

translations.literal: ” An angry, thereupon killed him.
translations.idiomatic: ” Chen An, enraged, executed him.

sentences.zh: 以魯憑為參軍，又遣其弟集及將軍張明等率騎二萬追曜，曜衛軍呼延瑜逆戰，擊斬之，悉俘其眾。

translations.literal: He made Lu Ping army adviser, also sent younger brother Ji and general Zhang Ming and others to lead twenty thousand horse to pursue Yao; Yao’s guard-army Huyan Yu met battle, struck and beheaded them, wholly took prisoner their host.
translations.idiomatic: He appointed Lu Ping as staff adviser and sent his brother Chen Ji, Zhang Ming, and twenty thousand riders after Liu Yao. Huyan Yu, captain of the imperial guard, rode out, cut them down, and captured the entire column.

sentences.zh: 安懼，馳還上邽。

translations.literal: An feared, galloped back to Shanggui.
translations.idiomatic: Terror-stricken, Chen An raced back to Shanggui.

sentences.zh: 曜至自南安。

translations.literal: Yao arrived from Nan’an.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Yao returned alive from Nan’an.

sentences.zh: 陳安使其將劉烈、趙罕襲汧城，拔之，西州氐羌悉從安。

translations.literal: Chen An ordered his generals Liu Lie, Zhao Han to raid Qian city, uprooted it; western province Di and Qiang all followed An.
translations.idiomatic: Chen An sent Liu Lie and Zhao Han to storm Qian and take it, and every Di and Qiang clan west of the capital rallied to him.

sentences.zh: 安士馬雄盛，眾十餘萬，自稱使持節、大都督、假黃鉞、大將軍、雍涼秦梁四州牧、涼王，以趙募為相國，領左長史。

translations.literal: An’s soldiers and horses mighty-thriving, host more than one hundred thousand, self-titled bearer of credentials, grand area commander, false yellow axe, grand general, shepherd of four prefectures Yong, Liang, Qin, Liang, King of Liang, making Zhao Mu chancellor of state, concurrently left chief clerk.
translations.idiomatic: His army swelled past a hundred thousand. Chen An styled himself king of Liang, credential bearer, grand commander, holder of the yellow battle-axe, general-in-chief, and governor of Yong, Liang, Qin, and Liang, with Zhao Mu as chancellor and senior clerk of the left.

sentences.zh: 魯憑對安大哭曰：「吾不忍見陳安之死也。

translations.literal: Lu Ping to An greatly wept saying, “I cannot bear to see Chen An’s death.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Ping wailed at him, “I will not live to see your doom.

sentences.zh: 」安怒，命斬之。

translations.literal: ” An angry, ordered behead him.
translations.idiomatic: ” Chen An ordered him beheaded in fury.

sentences.zh: 憑曰：「死自吾分，懸吾頭于秦州通衢，觀趙之斬陳安也。

translations.literal: Ping said, “Death is my lot; suspend my head on Qinzhou’s highway, watch Zhao behead Chen An.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Ping said, “My death is fate; hang my head on the high road of Qinzhou and watch Zhao execute Chen An.

sentences.zh: 」遂殺之。

translations.literal: ” Thereupon killed him.
translations.idiomatic: ” They cut him down.

sentences.zh: 曜聞憑死，悲慟曰：「賢人者，天下之望也。

translations.literal: Yao heard Ping died, grieved and said, “Worthy men are the hope of all under heaven.
translations.idiomatic: When Liu Yao learned of Lu Ping’s death he mourned, “Men of worth are the hope of the realm.

sentences.zh: 害賢人，是塞天下之情，夫承平之君猶不敢乖臣妾之心，況于四海乎！

translations.literal: To harm worthy men is to block the feelings of all under heaven; husbands who inherit peace still dare not violate the hearts of servants and concubines—how much more within the four seas!
translations.idiomatic: To murder such a man chokes the world’s goodwill; even emperors at peace fear to wound a concubine’s heart—what of the whole empire?

sentences.zh: 陳安今於招賢采哲之秋，而害君子，絕當時之望，吾知其無能為也。」

translations.literal: Chen An now in the autumn of summoning worthies and gathering sages, yet harms gentlemen, cuts off the hope of the time—I know he cannot accomplish anything.”
translations.idiomatic: Chen An, at the very hour when he should gather wise men, slays the virtuous and forfeits every expectation—I know he is finished.”

sentences.zh: 休屠王石武以桑城降，曜大悅，署武為使持節、都督秦州隴上雜夷諸軍事、平西大將軍、秦州刺史，封酒泉王。

translations.literal: Xiutu king Shi Wu with Sang city submitted; Yao greatly pleased, appointed Wu bearer of credentials, area commander Qinzhou Long upland miscellaneous Yi all military affairs, Pacifier-of-the-West grand general, Qinzhou inspector, enfeoffed Prince of Jiuquan.
translations.idiomatic: The Xiutu prince Shi Wu surrendered Sangcheng. Delighted, Liu Yao named him west-pacifying commander-in-chief, governor of Qin, prince of Jiuquan, and gave him the yellow axe over the mixed tribes of the Long marches.

sentences.zh: 曜-{后}-羊氏死，偽諡獻文皇后。

translations.literal: Yao’s empress Lady Yang died, falsely posthumous titled Empress Xianwen.
translations.idiomatic: Empress Yang died and received the posthumous title Empress Xianwen.

sentences.zh: 羊氏內有特寵，外參朝政，生曜三子熙、襲、闡。

translations.literal: Lady Yang within had special favor, without joined court governance, bore Yao three sons Xi, Xi, Chan.
translations.idiomatic: Lady Yang enjoyed unrivaled favor within the palace and a voice in government; she bore Liu Yao three sons—Xi, Xí, and Chan.

sentences.zh: 曜始禁無官者不聽乘馬，祿八百石已上婦女乃得衣錦繡，自季秋農功畢，乃聽飲酒，非宗廟社稷之祭不得殺牛，犯者皆死。

translations.literal: Yao first forbade those without office not permitted to ride horses; salary eight hundred shi and above women then could wear brocade embroidery; from late autumn when farming work finished, then permitted drinking wine; except ancestral temple and altars sacrifices not permitted to kill oxen—violators all died.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Yao first barred commoners without rank from riding horses; only households salaried at eight hundred piculs or more might dress their women in brocade. Drinking was allowed only after the harvest; cattle could be slaughtered solely for state sacrifices, and any other kill meant death.

sentences.zh: 曜臨太學，引試學生之上第者拜郎中。

translations.literal: Yao attended the Grand Academy, led and tested students of upper grade, appointed them gentlemen of the palace.
translations.idiomatic: He visited the academy, examined the highest-ranked students, and named them gentlemen of the palace.

sentences.zh: 武功男子蘇撫、陝男子伍長平並化為女子。

translations.literal: Wugong man Su Fu, Shan man Wu Changping both transformed into women.
translations.idiomatic: In Wugong a man named Su Fu and in Shan a man named Wu Changping turned into women.

sentences.zh: 石言於陝，若言勿東者。

translations.literal: Stone spoke at Shan, as if saying do not east.
translations.idiomatic: At Shan a stone was said to speak, as though warning, “Do not march east.”

sentences.zh: 曜將葬其父及妻，親如粟邑以規度之。

translations.literal: Yao about to bury his father and wife, personally went to Suyi to plan measure them.
translations.idiomatic: Preparing to bury his father and empress, Liu Yao went in person to Suyi to lay out the works.

sentences.zh: 負土為墳，其下周回二里，作者繼以脂燭，怨呼之聲盈于道路。

translations.literal: Shouldering earth made mound; below its circuit two li; workers succeeded one another with grease candles; resentful cries filled the roads.
translations.idiomatic: Laborers shouldered earth until the barrow ran two li around, toiling by torchlight while groans of resentment filled the roads.

sentences.zh: 遊子遠諫曰：「臣聞聖主明王、忠臣孝子之于終葬也，棺足周身，槨足周棺，藏足周槨而已，不封不樹，為無窮這計。

translations.literal: You Ziyuan remonstrated saying, “We have heard sage lords and enlightened kings, loyal ministers and filial sons regarding final burial: coffin suffices to wrap the body, outer coffin suffices to wrap coffin, concealment suffices to wrap outer coffin—that is all; not mound not tree, acting for endless this plan.
translations.idiomatic: You Ziyuan urged, “Sage kings and dutiful sons know burial needs only a coffin within a shell within a pit, without heaping earth or planting trees—planning for eternity.

sentences.zh: 伏惟陛下聖慈幽被，神鑒洞遠，每以清儉恤下為先。

translations.literal: We humbly consider Your Majesty sage-kindness darkly overspreads, spirit-mirror penetrating far, always taking clear thrift and pitying those below as first.
translations.idiomatic: Your majesty is famed for compassion and frugality toward the people.

sentences.zh: 社稷資儲為本。

translations.literal: Altars and grain rely on stores as root.
translations.idiomatic: The altars of soil and grain rest on the treasury.

sentences.zh: 今二陵之費至以億計，計六萬夫百日作，所用六百萬功。

translations.literal: Now the two mausoleums’ expense reaches to yi count; reckoned sixty thousand men one hundred days’ work, used six million labor-units.
translations.idiomatic: Yet these two tombs will cost hundreds of millions, needing sixty thousand laborers for a hundred days—six million man-days.

sentences.zh: 二陵皆下錮三泉，上崇百尺，積石為山，增土為阜，發掘古塚以千百數，役夫呼嗟，氣塞天地，暴骸原野，哭聲盈衢，臣竊謂無益於先皇先-{后}-，而徒喪國之儲力。

translations.literal: Both mausoleums below fix three springs, above rise one hundred chi, pile stone as mountains, add earth as mounds, opened dug ancient tombs by thousand-hundred count; laborers wail, qi blocks heaven and earth; expose bones in wilds, crying voices fill crossroads; your servant privately says no benefit to late emperor and late empress, but in vain loses the state’s stored strength.
translations.idiomatic: Both sink shafts to the three streams and rear mounds a hundred feet high, piling stone into artificial hills and rifling countless old graves. The workers’ laments choke heaven; bones litter the fields and keening fills the highways. I say this profits neither your late father nor empress but bleeds the realm dry.

sentences.zh: 陛下脫仰尋堯舜之軌者，則功不盈百萬，費亦不過千計，下無怨骨，上無怨人，先帝先-{后}-有太山之安，陛下饗舜、禹、周公之美，惟陛下察焉。

translations.literal: Your Majesty if upward trace Yao and Shun’s tracks, then accomplishment not exceeding one million, expense also not passing thousand count; below no resentful bones, above no resentful people; late emperor and late empress have Mount Tai’s peace; Your Majesty enjoys Shun, Yu, Duke of Zhou’s beauty—only may Your Majesty examine it.
translations.idiomatic: Follow Yao and Shun’s example and the cost falls below a million, the toll below a thousand families, with no resentful dead above or below; your parents rest secure as Mount Tai while you earn a name beside Shun, Yu, and the Duke of Zhou. I beg you to consider this.”

sentences.zh: 」曜不納，乃使其將劉岳等帥騎一萬，迎父及弟暉喪于太原。

translations.literal: ” Yao did not accept; then ordered his general Liu Yue and others to command ten thousand horse, welcome father and younger brother Hui’s remains at Taiyuan.
translations.idiomatic: ” Liu Yao refused. He sent Liu Yue with ten thousand horsemen to fetch his father’s coffin and that of his brother Liu Hui from Taiyuan.

sentences.zh: 疫氣大行，死者十三四。

translations.literal: Epidemic qi greatly moved; dead thirteen or four in ten.
translations.idiomatic: Plague swept the army, killing three or four men in ten.

sentences.zh: 上洛男子張盧死二十七日，有盜發其塚者，盧得蘇。

translations.literal: Shangluo man Zhang Lu died twenty-seven days; there was a robber who opened his tomb; Lu revived.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Lu of Shangluo had been dead twenty-seven days when grave robbers opened his mound—and he sat up alive.

sentences.zh: 曜葬其父，墓號永垣陵，葬妻羊氏，墓號顯平陵。
