translations.literal: Yao buried his father, tomb titled Yongyuan Mausoleum; buried wife Lady Yang, tomb titled Xianping Mausoleum.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Yao interred his father in the Yongyuan tomb and Empress Yang in the Xianping tomb.

sentences.zh: 大赦境內殊死巳下，賜人爵二級，孤老貧病不能自存者帛各有差。

translations.literal: Greatly amnestied within borders short of capital death, gifted people two ranks of nobility, orphans elderly poor sick unable self-preserve silk each had gradation.
translations.idiomatic: He proclaimed a general amnesty short of capital crimes, raised commoners two degrees in rank, and distributed silk in graded amounts to widows, elders, and the destitute.

sentences.zh: 太甯元年，陳安攻曜征西劉貢于南安，休屠王石武自桑城將攻上邽，以解南安之圍。

translations.literal: First year of Taining, Chen An attacked Yao’s west-conquering Liu Gong at Nan’an; Xiutu king Shi Wu from Sang city was about to attack Shanggui, thereby relieving Nan’an’s siege.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of the Taining era Chen An besieged Liu Gong, Liu Yao’s west-conquering general, at Nan’an. Shi Wu the Xiutu king marched from Sangcheng toward Shanggui to lift the pressure on Nan’an.

sentences.zh: 安聞之懼，馳歸上邽，遇于瓜田。

translations.literal: An heard it feared, galloped back to Shanggui, met at Guatian.
translations.idiomatic: Chen An, alarmed, galloped toward Shanggui and met him at Guatian.

sentences.zh: 武以眾寡不敵，奔保張春故壘。

translations.literal: Wu because host few could not match enemy, fled and held Zhang Chun’s old fort.
translations.idiomatic: Outnumbered, Shi Wu fell back to Zhang Chun’s old fortress.

sentences.zh: 安引軍追武曰：「叛逆胡奴！

translations.literal: An led army pursuing Wu saying, “Rebel Hu slave!
translations.idiomatic: Chen An pursued, shouting, “Rebel Hu dog!

sentences.zh: 要當生縛此奴，然後斬劉貢。

translations.literal: Essential will alive bind this slave, then behead Liu Gong.
translations.idiomatic: I will take you alive before I deal with Liu Gong.

sentences.zh: 」武閉壘距之。

translations.literal: ” Wu closed fort resisted him.
translations.idiomatic: ” Shi Wu barred the gates and held him off.

sentences.zh: 貢敗安後軍，俘斬萬餘。

translations.literal: Gong defeated An’s rear army, captured and beheaded more than ten thousand.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Gong crushed Chen An’s rear guard and killed or captured over ten thousand.

sentences.zh: 安馳還赴救，貢逆擊敗之。

translations.literal: An galloped back to rush rescue; Gong met attack and defeated him.
translations.idiomatic: Chen An wheeled about to save the day; Liu Gong intercepted him and broke his charge.

sentences.zh: 俄而武騎大至，安眾大潰，收騎八千，奔於隴城。

translations.literal: Soon Wu’s horse great arrived; An’s host greatly collapsed; gathered horse eight thousand, fled to Long city.
translations.idiomatic: Then Shi Wu’s cavalry arrived in force; Chen An’s army collapsed. He salvaged eight thousand riders and bolted for Longcheng.

sentences.zh: 貢乃留武督後眾，躬先士卒，戰輒敗之，遂圍安於隴城。

translations.literal: Gong then left Wu to supervise rear host, personally led ahead soldiers and men, battle always defeated them, thereupon surrounded An at Long city.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Gong left Shi Wu with the rearguard, led the van himself, and drove Chen An back until he had him bottled up in Longcheng.

sentences.zh: 大雨霖，震曜父墓門屋，大風飄發其父寢堂于垣外五十餘步。

translations.literal: Great rain long; thunder shook Yao father tomb gate-house; great wind blew and uprooted his father’s sleep-hall beyond the wall fifty-plus paces.
translations.idiomatic: Torrential rains fell; lightning shattered the gatehouse of Liu Yao’s father’s tomb and a gale tore the memorial hall from its foundations and cast it fifty paces outside the wall.

sentences.zh: 曜避正殿，素服哭於東堂五日，使其鎮軍劉襲、太常梁胥等繕復之。

translations.literal: Yao avoided main hall, in plain clothes wept in eastern hall five days, ordered his stabilizing-army Liu Xi, grand master of rituals Liang Xu and others to repair restore it.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Yao quit the main hall, wore undyed mourning in the eastern hall for five days, and told Liu Xi, captain of the guard, and Liang Xu, grand master of rites, to rebuild the shrine.

sentences.zh: 松柏眾木植已成林，至是悉枯。

translations.literal: Pine cypress many trees planted already became forest; by this all withered.
translations.idiomatic: The pines and cypresses planted there had grown into a wood; now they withered to the last tree.

sentences.zh: 署其大司馬劉雅為太宰，加劍履上殿，入朝不趨，贊拜不名，給千兵百騎，甲仗百人入殿，增班劍六十人，前後鼓吹各二部。

translations.literal: He appointed his grand minister of war Liu Ya as grand tutor, added sword and shoes ascending hall, entering court not hastening, praised bow not naming, supplied thousand soldiers hundred horse, armored guards hundred men entering hall, increased class sword sixty men, front and rear drum-flute each two sections.
translations.idiomatic: He promoted Liu Ya to grand tutor with the honors of wearing sword and shoes in the hall, walking slowly at court, and being hailed without his name, gave him a thousand guards, a hundred household cavalry, a hundred armored attendants in the palace, sixty escort swordsmen, and two bands of music before and behind.

sentences.zh: 曜親征陳安，圍安於隴城。

translations.literal: Yao personally campaigned Chen An, surrounded An at Long city.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Yao took the field in person and invested Chen An in Longcheng.

sentences.zh: 安頻出挑戰，累擊敗之，斬獲八千餘級。

translations.literal: An repeatedly came out challenging, repeatedly struck and defeated him, beheaded and captured eight thousand-plus heads.
translations.idiomatic: Chen An sallied again and again; each time Liu Yao threw him back, taking more than eight thousand heads.

sentences.zh: 右軍劉幹攻平襄，克之，隴上諸縣悉降。

translations.literal: Right army Liu Gan attacked Pingxiang, overcame it; Long upland various counties all submitted.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Gan’s right wing stormed Pingxiang and every county on the Long plateau submitted.

sentences.zh: 曲赦隴右殊死已下，惟陳安、趙募不在其例。

translations.literal: Curved amnesty Long right short of capital death below, only Chen An, Zhao Mu not in the precedent.
translations.idiomatic: He offered a limited amnesty west of the Long passes—everyone but Chen An and Zhao Mu.

sentences.zh: 安留楊伯支、姜沖兒等守隴城，帥騎數百突圍而出，欲引上邽、平襄之眾還解隴城之圍。

translations.literal: An left Yang Bozhi, Jiang Chong’er and others guarding Long city, led several hundred horse broke siege and out, wished to lead Shanggui, Pingxiang’s host back to relieve Long city’s siege.
translations.idiomatic: Chen An left Yang Bozhi and Jiang Chong’er to hold Longcheng, broke out with a few hundred horsemen, and tried to rally the forces of Shanggui and Pingxiang to lift the siege.

sentences.zh: 安既出，知上邽被圍，平襄已敗，乃南走陝中。

translations.literal: An having exited, knew Shanggui was surrounded, Pingxiang already defeated, then south fled into Shanzhong.
translations.idiomatic: Learning that Shanggui was surrounded and Pingxiang lost, he fled south into the gorges of Shan.

sentences.zh: 曜使其將軍平先、丘中伯率勁騎追安，頻戰敗之，俘斬四百餘級。

translations.literal: Yao ordered generals Ping Xian, Qiu Zhongbo to lead keen horse pursue An, repeatedly battled defeated him, captured beheaded four hundred-plus heads.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Yao sent Ping Xian and Qiu Zhongbo with elite cavalry in pursuit, repeatedly defeated him, and killed or captured more than four hundred.

sentences.zh: 安與壯士十餘騎於陝中格戰，安左手奮七尺大刀，右手執丈八蛇矛，近交則刀矛俱發，輒害五六；

translations.literal: An with stalwart men ten-some horse in Shanzhong fought hand-to-hand; An left hand wielded seven-chi great knife, right hand grasped one zhang eight snake-spear; near clash then knife and spear both issued, always harmed five or six;
translations.idiomatic: With a dozen riders Chen An made a stand in the defiles, swinging a seven-foot saber in his left hand and an eighteen-foot serpent spear in his right; at close range blade and lance flashed together, felling five or six foes at a blow;

sentences.zh: 遠則雙帶鞬服，左右馳射而走。

translations.literal: far then double belt quiver case, left and right gallop shoot and run.
translations.idiomatic: at distance he slung paired quivers and shot from the saddle as he wheeled away.

sentences.zh: 平先亦壯健絕人，勇捷如飛，與安搏戰，三交，奪其蛇矛而退。

translations.literal: Ping Xian also stalwart strong surpassing others, brave swift like flying, with An grapple-fought, three exchanges, seized his snake-spear and withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: Ping Xian was himself a marvel of strength and speed; he closed with Chen Ant three passes, tore away the serpent spear, and broke off.

sentences.zh: 會日暮，雨甚，安棄馬，與左右五六人步逾山嶺，匿於溪澗。

translations.literal: Meeting sun dusk, rain very heavy, An abandoned horse, with left and right five-six men walked over mountain ridge, hid in stream gully.
translations.idiomatic: Night fell and rain sheeted down; Chen An abandoned his mount and slipped into the hills with five or six followers, hiding in a ravine.

sentences.zh: 翌日尋之，遂不知所在。

translations.literal: Next day searched him, thereupon did not know where located.
translations.idiomatic: Next day’s search found no trace.

sentences.zh: 會連雨始霽，輔威呼延清尋其徑跡，斬安于澗曲。

translations.literal: Meeting continuous rain beginning clear, auxiliary-prestige Huyan Qing sought his path-tracks, beheaded An in stream bend.
translations.idiomatic: When the rains finally broke, Huyan Qing, general of auxiliary prestige, picked up his trail and slew Chen An in a creek bend.

sentences.zh: 曜大悅。

translations.literal: Yao greatly pleased.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Yao was elated.

sentences.zh: 安善於撫接，吉凶夷險與眾同之，及其死，隴上歌之曰：「隴上壯士有陳安，驅幹雖小腹中寬，愛養將士同心肝。

translations.literal: An was good at comforting and receiving, auspicious and inauspicious, level and perilous with the host the same; at his death, Long upland sang him saying, “Long upland stalwart has Chen An, trunk stem though small belly inside wide, loving and nurturing generals and soldiers same heart liver.
translations.idiomatic: Chen An had a gift for winning men; he shared every fortune and hardship with his troops. After he died the people of Long sang: “On the Long plateau the hero was Chen An—slight of frame but broad of heart, who fed his soldiers like kin.

sentences.zh: 䯀驄父馬鐵瑕鞍，七尺大刀奮如湍，丈八蛇矛左右盤，十蕩十決無當前。

translations.literal: Lean-collion sire horse iron flaw saddle, seven-chi great knife rushes like rapid, one zhang eight snake-spear left and right coil, ten charges ten decisions none before.
translations.idiomatic: His dapple sire bore iron-trimmed tack; his seven-foot blade flashed like a torrent, his eighteen-foot serpent spear danced right and left; ten charges, ten breakthroughs, and none could stand before him.

sentences.zh: 戰始三交失蛇矛，棄我䯀驄竄嚴幽，為我外援而懸頭。

translations.literal: Battle began three exchanges lost snake-spear, abandoned my lean-collion fled crag gloom, for me outer aid yet head suspended.
translations.idiomatic: Three passes into the fight he lost the spear, abandoned his dapple steed in the rocky dark—though he sought outside help they took his head.

sentences.zh: 西流之水東流河，一去不還奈子何！

translations.literal: West-flowing water east-flowing river, one gone not return what can you do!
translations.idiomatic: The western stream runs east into the river—gone, never to return—what can we do for you?”

sentences.zh: 」曜聞而嘉傷，命樂府歌之。

translations.literal: ” Yao heard and praised and grieved, ordered music bureau to sing it.
translations.idiomatic: ” Liu Yao heard the dirge, was moved, and had the imperial musicians perform it.

sentences.zh: 楊伯支斬姜沖兒，以隴城降。

translations.literal: Yang Bozhi beheaded Jiang Chong’er, with Long city submitted.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Bozhi killed Jiang Chong’er and surrendered Longcheng.

sentences.zh: 宋亭斬趙募，以上邽降。

translations.literal: Song Ting beheaded Zhao Mu, with Shanggui submitted.
translations.idiomatic: Song Ting slew Zhao Mu and opened Shanggui.

sentences.zh: 徙秦州大姓楊、姜諸族二千餘戶于長安。

translations.literal: Moved Qinzhou great clans Yang, Jiang various families two thousand-plus households to Chang’an.
translations.idiomatic: More than two thousand households of the Yang, Jiang, and other great clans of Qinzhou were relocated to Chang’an.

sentences.zh: 氐羌悉下，並送質任。

translations.literal: Di and Qiang all submitted, together sent hostages.
translations.idiomatic: The Di and Qiang capitulated and sent hostages.

sentences.zh: 時劉岳與涼州刺史張茂相持於河上，曜自隴長驅至西河，戎卒二十八萬五千，臨河列營，百餘里中，鐘鼓之聲沸河動地，自古軍旅之盛未有斯比。

translations.literal: At the time Liu Yue and Liangzhou inspector Zhang Mao faced each other at the river; Yao from Long long-galloped to Xihe, Rong soldiers two hundred eighty-five thousand, along river arrayed camps, within hundred-plus li, bell-drum sounds boiled river shook earth; from antiquity army travel’s splendor never had this comparison.
translations.idiomatic: While Liu Yue and Zhang Mao, governor of Liangzhou, glared at each other across the Yellow River, Liu Yao swept down from the Long road to Xihe with two hundred eighty-five thousand tribal troops. Camps lined the bank for a hundred li; drums and bells shook the water—never had a host marched in such pomp.

sentences.zh: 茂臨河諸戍皆望風奔退。

translations.literal: Mao’s along-river various garrisons all saw wind and fled retreated.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Mao’s riverside posts fled at the rumor alone.

sentences.zh: 揚聲欲百道俱渡，直至姑臧，涼州大怖，人無固志。

translations.literal: Raised sound wishing hundred roads together ford, straight to Guzang; Liangzhou greatly terrified, people without firm resolve.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Yao boasted he would cross everywhere at once and march on Guzang; terror gripped Liangzhou and morale collapsed.

sentences.zh: 諸將咸欲速濟，曜曰：「吾軍旅雖盛，不逾魏武之東也。

translations.literal: Generals all wished speed ford; Yao said, “Our army travel though splendid, not exceeding Wei Wu’s east.
translations.idiomatic: His generals urged an immediate crossing. Liu Yao said, “This host, grand as it is, is no larger than Cao Cao’s eastern campaigns.

sentences.zh: 畏威而來者，三有二焉。

translations.literal: Those who come fearing might, two of three are such.
translations.idiomatic: Two men in three march only because they fear us.

sentences.zh: 中軍宿衛已皆疲老，不可用也。

translations.literal: Middle army night-guards already all weary old, not usable.
translations.idiomatic: The palace guard is worn out and useless.

sentences.zh: 張氏以吾新平陳安，師徒殷盛，以形聲言之，非彼五郡之眾所能抗也，必怖而歸命，受制稱籓，吾復何求！

translations.literal: Zhang clan takes Us newly pacified Chen An, army followers abundant thriving, by form and sound speaking, not that five commanderies’ host able to resist, certain terrified and submit fate, receive control declare vassalage—what else do We seek!
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Mao thinks us fresh from crushing Chen An and swollen with might; in plain sight his five commanderies cannot stand against us. He will panic, offer submission, and bend the knee—what more could I want?

sentences.zh: 卿等試之，不出中旬，張茂之表不至者，吾為負卿矣。

translations.literal: You gentlemen try it; if not exiting mid-month, Zhang Mao’s memorial not arrive, We will have failed you.
translations.idiomatic: Wait: if by mid-month his petition of surrender has not come, blame me.

sentences.zh: 」茂懼，果遣使稱籓，獻馬一千五百匹，牛三千頭，羊十萬口，黃金三百八十斤，銀七百斤，女妓二十人，及諸珍寶珠玉、方域美貨不可勝紀。

translations.literal: ” Mao feared, indeed sent envoy declaring vassalage, presented horses one thousand five hundred head, oxen three thousand head, sheep one hundred thousand mouth, yellow gold three hundred eighty jin, silver seven hundred jin, female entertainers twenty persons, and various precious treasures pearl jade, regional fine goods beyond record.
translations.idiomatic: ” Zhang Mao, frightened, dispatched envoys with fifteen hundred horses, three thousand oxen, a hundred thousand sheep, three hundred eighty catties of gold, seven hundred of silver, twenty singing girls, and treasures beyond counting.

sentences.zh: 曜大悅，使其大鴻臚田崧署茂使持節、假黃鉞、侍中、都督涼南北秦梁益巴漢隴右西域雜夷匈奴諸軍事、太師、領大司馬、涼州牧、領西域大都護、護氐羌校尉、涼王。

translations.literal: Yao greatly pleased, ordered his grand herald Tian Song to appoint Mao bearer of credentials, false yellow axe, palace attendant, area commander Liang south north Qin Liang Yi Ba Han Long right Western Regions miscellaneous Yi Xiongnu all military affairs, grand preceptor, concurrently grand minister of war, Liangzhou shepherd, concurrently grand protector Western Regions, protector Di Qiang colonel, King of Liang.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Yao charged his herald Tian Song to invest Zhang Mao with credentials, the yellow axe, and a vast bundle of military and civil titles—grand preceptor, grand minister of war, governor of Liang, protector-general of the Western Regions, colonel of the Di and Qiang, and king of Liang.

sentences.zh: 曜至自河西，遣胡元增其父及妻墓高九十尺。

translations.literal: Yao arrived from Hexi, sent Hu Yuan to raise his father and wife tombs ninety chi.
translations.idiomatic: Returning from the Hexi expedition, he sent Hu Yuan to raise his father’s and empress’s mounds ninety chi higher.

sentences.zh: 楊難敵以陳安既平，內懷危懼，奔於漢中。

translations.literal: Yang Nan-di because Chen An already pacified, within cherished peril fear, fled to Hanzhong.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Nan-di, terrified now that Chen An was gone, bolted for Hanzhong.

sentences.zh: 鎮西劉厚追擊之，獲其輜重千餘兩，士女六千餘人，還之仇池。

translations.literal: Pacifier-of-the-West Liu Hou pursued struck him, obtained his baggage train more than one thousand liang, gentlemen and women six thousand-plus persons, returned them to Chouci.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Hou, west-pacifying general, overtook him, seized more than a thousand cartloads of baggage and six thousand captives, and restored them to Chouci.

sentences.zh: 曜以大鴻臚田崧為鎮南大將軍、益州刺史，鎮仇池，以劉嶽為侍中、都督中外諸軍事，進封中山王。

translations.literal: Yao made grand herald Tian Song Pacifier-of-the-South grand general, Yi prefecture inspector, garrison Chouci; made Liu Yue palace attendant, area commander all military within and without, advanced enfeoffed Prince of Zhongshan.
translations.idiomatic: He named Tian Song south-pacifying commander-in-chief and governor of Yi, stationed at Chouci, and made Liu Yue palace attendant and commander-in-chief of all armies, elevating him to prince of Zhongshan.

sentences.zh: 初，靳准之亂，曜世子胤沒于黑匿郁鞠部，至是，胤自言，郁鞠大驚，資給衣馬，遣子送之。

translations.literal: At first, at Jin Zhun’s turmoil, Yao’s heir son Yin was lost in Heini Yuju’s section; reaching this, Yin self-spoke; Yuju greatly startled, supplied clothes horses, sent son escorted him.
translations.idiomatic: During Jin Zhun’s coup the heir Liu Yin had fallen among the tribes of Heini Yuju. Now he revealed himself; the chief, astonished, clothed and mounted him and sent his own son as escort.

sentences.zh: 曜對胤悲慟，嘉郁鞠忠款，署使持節、散騎常侍、忠義大將軍、左賢王。

translations.literal: Yao facing Yin grieved greatly, praised Yuju loyal sincerity, appointed bearer of credentials, unattached cavalry attendant, loyally righteous grand general, left worthy king.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Yao wept over his son and rewarded Yuju’s loyalty with credentials, the title of loyal and righteous commander-in-chief, and kingship of the left worthy horde.

sentences.zh: 胤字義孫，美姿貌，善機對，年十歲，身長七尺五寸，眉鬢如畫。

translations.literal: Yin courtesy name Yisun, handsome bearing, skilled at opportune replies; age ten, body seven chi five cun, eyebrows and sideburns like painting.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Yin, courtesy Yisun, was handsome, quick of wit, stood seven feet five at age ten, and had brows and whiskers like ink paintings.

sentences.zh: 聰奇之，謂曜曰：「此兒神氣豈同義真乎！

translations.literal: Cong marvelled at him, said to Yao, “This child’s spirit-breath how same Yizhen!
translations.idiomatic: Liu Cong exclaimed to Liu Yao, “The boy’s aura is nothing like Yizhen’s!

sentences.zh: 固當應為卿之塚嫡，卿可思文王廢伯邑考立武王之意也。

translations.literal: Solid ought to become your legitimate heir; you can ponder King Wen’s deposing Bo Yikao and establishing King Wu’s meaning.
translations.idiomatic: He should be your true successor—remember how King Wen passed over Bo Yikao for King Wu.

sentences.zh: 」曜曰：「臣之籓國，僅能守祭祀便足矣，不可以亂長幼之倫也。

translations.literal: ” Yao said, “Your servant’s fief state, only able to guard sacrifices then suffices, cannot thereby disorder elder-younger’s bonds.
translations.idiomatic: ” Liu Yao replied, “My fief needs only someone to tend the sacrifices; I will not upset the order of age among my sons.

sentences.zh: 」聰曰：「卿勳格天地，國兼百城，當世祚太師，受專征之任，五侯九伯得專征之者，卿之子孫，柰何言同諸籓國也！

translations.literal: ” Cong said, “Your merit reaches heaven and earth, the state joins a hundred cities; you ought receive generation’s fortune as grand preceptor, receive special campaign’s charge—those five marquises and nine earls who obtained special-campaign power were your sons and grandsons—how speak the same as various fief states!
translations.idiomatic: ” Liu Cong replied, “Your deeds span heaven and earth and your domain spans a hundred cities; you should rank as grand preceptor with plenary war powers, as did the ancient marquises who led their own campaigns—your heirs will inherit that authority. How can you compare yourself to an ordinary vassal?

sentences.zh: 義真既不能遠追太伯高讓之風，吾不過為卿封之以一國。

translations.literal: Yizhen since cannot far pursue Taibo’s high-yielding wind, We only pass for you enfeoffing him with one state.
translations.idiomatic: Since Yizhen cannot rival Taibo’s selfless abdication, I can at most enfeoff him with a single principality.

sentences.zh: 」義真，曜子儉之字也。

translations.literal: ” Yizhen was Yao son Jian’s courtesy name.
translations.idiomatic: ” “Yizhen” was the courtesy name of Liu Yao’s son Liu Jian.

sentences.zh: 於是封儉為臨海王，立胤為世子。

translations.literal: Thereupon enfeoffed Jian as Prince of Linhai, established Yin as heir apparent.
translations.idiomatic: He therefore created Liu Jian prince of Linhai and named Liu Yin heir apparent.

sentences.zh: 胤雖少離屯難，流躓殊荒，而風骨俊茂，爽朗卓然；

translations.literal: Yin though young parted from hardship and crisis, drifted and stumbled in utterly wild lands, yet wind-bones handsome-thriving, bright and open outstanding;
translations.idiomatic: Though Liu Yin had been lost in exile since boyhood, he grew tall in spirit—clear-eyed and striking.

sentences.zh: 身長八尺三寸，發與身齊，多力善射，驍捷如風雲，曜因以重之，其朝臣亦屬意焉。

translations.literal: body eight chi three cun tall, hair level with body, much strength skilled at shooting, fierce swift like wind and cloud; Yao therefore valued him, his court ministers also fixed hopes on him.
translations.idiomatic: He stood eight feet three inches, hair sweeping to his shoulders, immensely strong and a superb archer, swift as a storm. Liu Yao doted on him, and the court looked to him as well.

sentences.zh: 曜於是顧謂群下曰：「義孫可謂歲寒而不凋，涅而不淄者矣。

translations.literal: Yao thereupon turned and said to the host below, “Yisun can be called not withering in year’s cold, not blackening in mud.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Yao told his officials, “Yisun is like pine in winter or lacquer in dye—unbowed by hardship.

sentences.zh: 義光雖先已樹立，然沖幼儒謹，恐難乎為今世之儲貳也，懼非所以上固社稷，下愛義光。

translations.literal: Yiguang though before already established, yet young, Confucian-cautious; I fear hard to be this age’s heir-apparent; fear not what thereby above secures altars, below loves Yiguang.
translations.idiomatic: Yiguang was named crown prince first, but he is still a timid child; I fear he cannot serve as heir in these times, to the peril of the realm and of his own welfare.

sentences.zh: 義孫年長明德，又先世子也，朕欲遠追周文，近蹤光武，使宗廟有太山之安，義光饗無疆之福，于諸卿意如何？

translations.literal: Yisun elder in years, bright in virtue, again former heir son; We wish far pursue King Wen of Zhou, near trace Guangwu, causing ancestral temple to have Mount Tai’s peace, Yiguang to enjoy boundless fortune—what do the various gentlemen think?
translations.idiomatic: Yisun is older, virtuous, and was always the designated successor. I mean to follow King Wen of Zhou and Emperor Guangwu of Han so the temple stands firm as Mount Tai and Yiguang enjoys lasting blessing—what say you?”

sentences.zh: 」其太傅呼延晏等咸曰：「陛下遠擬周漢，為國家無窮之計，豈惟臣等賴之，實亦宗廟四海之慶。

translations.literal: ” His grand tutor Huyan Yan and others all said, “Your Majesty far models Zhou and Han, acting for the state’s endless plan—not only do we ministers rely on it, truly it is also the altars’ and four seas’ rejoicing.
translations.idiomatic: ” Grand Tutor Huyan Yan and the rest answered, “By looking to Zhou and Han you secure the dynasty for ages—this gladdens not only your servants but all under heaven.

sentences.zh: 」左光祿卜泰、太子太保韓廣等進曰：「陛下若以廢立為是也，則不應降日月之明，垂訪群下。

translations.literal: ” Left grand master Bu Tai, crown prince grand guardian Han Guang and others advanced saying, “Your Majesty if take deposition and establishment as right, then ought not lower sun and moon’s brightness, hang inquiry on the host below.
translations.idiomatic: ” Bu Tai, Han Guang, and others stepped forward: “If the change were plainly just, you would not need to dim your own radiance by polling the court.

sentences.zh: 若以為疑也，固思聞臣等異同之言，竊以誠廢太子非也。

translations.literal: If take as doubt, solidly wish hear your servants’ differing and agreeing words; privately deem truly deposing the heir is not right.
translations.idiomatic: If you still doubt, you must hear opposing views—and we hold that deposing the crown prince is wrong.

sentences.zh: 何則？

translations.literal: Why so?
translations.idiomatic: Why?

sentences.zh: 昔周文以未建之前，擇聖表而超樹之可也。

translations.literal: Formerly King Wen, before not yet establishing, choosing sage signs and surpassing establishing him was permissible.
translations.idiomatic: King Wen of Zhou could elevate a younger son before any heir was fixed, when heaven’s signs singled him out.

sentences.zh: 光武緣母色而廢立，豈足為聖朝之模範！

translations.literal: Guangwu followed mother’s beauty and deposed and established—how sufficient to be sage court’s model!
translations.idiomatic: Guangwu set aside an heir for a favorite’s son—hardly a precedent this court should follow!

sentences.zh: 光武誠以東海篡統，何必不如明帝！

translations.literal: Guangwu truly because Eastern Sea usurped succession—how must he not be equal to Ming Emperor!
translations.idiomatic: If Guangwu feared the prince of the Eastern Sea seizing the throne, that still does not prove the younger emperor outshone him!

sentences.zh: 皇子胤文武才略，神度弘遠，信獨絕一時，足以擬蹤周發；

translations.literal: Imperial son Yin civil and martial talent strategy, spirit measure vast and far, trust alone surpasses the age, sufficient to trace Zhou Fa;
translations.idiomatic: Prince Liu Yin’s civil and military gifts and far-reaching mind are unmatched; he could stand beside Fa of Zhou.

sentences.zh: 然太子孝友仁慈，志尚沖雅，亦足以堂負聖基，為承平之賢主。

translations.literal: Yet the crown prince filial, friendly, benevolent, humane, aims lofty and mild, also sufficient to hall-bear sacred foundation, be a heir-peace worthy lord.
translations.idiomatic: Yet the crown prince is filial, gentle, and humane—quite able to uphold the sacred line and rule wisely in tranquil times.

sentences.zh: 何況儲宮者，六合人神所系望也，不可輕以廢易。

translations.literal: How much more the heir’s palace is what six directions men and spirits tie hope to—cannot lightly by deposing change.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover the heir apparent is the cynosure of gods and men—you must not lightly cast him aside.

sentences.zh: 陛下誠實爾者，臣等有死而已，未敢奉詔。

translations.literal: Your Majesty truly solidly thus, your servants have death only, not dare receive edict.
translations.idiomatic: If you insist, we can only choose death—we cannot obey such an edict.”

sentences.zh: 」曜默然。

translations.literal: ” Yao silent.
translations.idiomatic: ” Liu Yao fell silent.

sentences.zh: 胤前泣曰：「慈父之于子也，當務存《屍鳩》之仁，何可替熙而立臣也！

translations.literal: Yin stepped forward weeping saying, “A kind father toward sons ought surely preserve the “Shi Jiu” kindness—how can replace Xi and establish your servant!
translations.idiomatic: Liu Yin came forward in tears: “A loving father should show the mercy praised in the ‘Cuckoo’ ode—how can you set aside Liu Xi for me!

sentences.zh: 陛下謬恩乃爾者，臣請死於此，以明赤心。

translations.literal: Your Majesty wrongly favoring thus, your servant begs die here, to clarify red heart.
translations.idiomatic: If this misplaced favor stands, let me die here and prove my loyalty.

sentences.zh: 且陛下若愛忘其醜，以臣微堪指授，亦當能輔導義光，仰遵聖軌。

translations.literal: Moreover Your Majesty if love forgets its ugliness, taking your servant slightly able instruct, also ought able assist guide Yiguang, upward follow sage tracks.
translations.idiomatic: Even if you think me fit to advise, I can still counsel Yiguang and keep him to the royal way.

sentences.zh: 」因歔欷流涕，悲感朝臣。

translations.literal: ” Thereupon sobbed and wept, grief moved court ministers.
translations.idiomatic: ” He broke down; the whole court wept with him.

sentences.zh: 曜亦以太子羊氏所生，羊有寵，哀之不忍廢，乃止。

translations.literal: Yao also because crown prince Yang clan bore, Yang had favor, pitied him not bear depose, then stopped.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Yao remembered that the crown prince was Lady Yang’s son and she still held his heart; he could not bear to cast the boy aside and dropped the plan.

sentences.zh: 追諡前妻卜氏為元悼皇后，胤之母也。

translations.literal: Posthumously titled former wife Lady Bu as Empress Yuan-dao, Yin’s mother.
translations.idiomatic: He posthumously honored his first consort Lady Bu, Liu Yin’s mother, as Empress Yuandao.

sentences.zh: 卜泰，胤之舅，曜嘉之，拜上光祿大夫、儀同三司、領太子太傅。

translations.literal: Bu Tai, Yin’s maternal uncle; Yao praised him, appointed senior grand master of golden seal, identical privy seal opening office, concurrently crown prince grand tutor.
translations.idiomatic: Bu Tai, Liu Yin’s uncle, won praise and was named senior grand master with three-duke privileges and tutor to the heir.

sentences.zh: 封胤為永安王，署侍中、衛大將軍、都督二宮禁衛諸軍事、開府儀同三司、錄尚書事，領太子太傅，號曰皇子。

translations.literal: Enfeoffed Yin as Prince of Yong’an, appointed palace attendant, guard grand general, area commander two palaces’ forbidden guard all military affairs, open office identical privy seal, recorder of secretariat affairs, concurrently crown prince grand tutor, titled imperial son.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Yin became prince of Yong’an, palace attendant, captain of the guard, commander of both palaces’ garrisons, recorder of affairs, and tutor to the heir, with full privy-seal honors, styled “imperial son.”

sentences.zh: 命熙于胤盡家人之禮。

translations.literal: Ordered Xi toward Yin perform full family ritual.
translations.idiomatic: He told Liu Xi to observe fraternal courtesy toward Liu Yin as if among common kin.

sentences.zh: 時有鳳皇將五子翔於故未央殿五日，悲鳴不食皆死。

translations.literal: At the time there was a phoenix about to lead five fledglings soaring over the old Weiyang Palace five days, sadly cried not eating, all died.
translations.idiomatic: A phoenix leading five chicks circled the ruins of Weiyang Palace for five days, wailing and fasting until all six perished.

sentences.zh: 曜立-{后}-劉氏。

translations.literal: Yao established empress Liu clan.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Yao enthroned Lady Liu as empress.

sentences.zh: 石勒將石他自雁門出上郡，襲安國將軍、北羌王盆句除，俘三千餘落，獲牛馬羊百餘萬而歸。

translations.literal: Shi Le’s general Shi Ta from Yanmen out to Shang commandery, raided stabilizing-the-state general, northern Qiang king Pen Juqu, captured three thousand-plus settlements, obtained oxen horses sheep one million-plus and returned.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Ta, Shi Le’s general, sortied from Yanmen into Shang commandery, fell upon Pen Juqu the northern Qiang king and stabilizing-the-state general, took more than three thousand camps, and drove home a million head of livestock.

sentences.zh: 曜大怒，投袂而起。

translations.literal: Yao greatly angry, cast sleeve and rose.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Yao flung down his sleeve and sprang up in fury.

sentences.zh: 是日次於渭城，遣劉嶽追之，曜次於富平，為嶽聲援。

translations.literal: That day halted at Weicheng, sent Liu Yue pursue him; Yao halted at Fuping, made sound aid for Yue.
translations.idiomatic: He camped that night at Weicheng and sent Liu Yue in pursuit while he himself stopped at Fuping to back the operation.

sentences.zh: 岳及石他戰於河濱，敗之，斬他及其甲士一千五百級，赴河死者五千餘人，悉收所虜，振旅而歸。

translations.literal: Yue and Shi Ta battled at river’s edge, defeated him, beheaded Ta and his armored soldiers one thousand five hundred grades, those who rushed river dead five thousand-plus persons, wholly gathered what was captured, shook troops and returned.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Yue caught Shi Ta on the riverbank, broke him, and took fifteen hundred heads; five thousand drowned fleeing. He recovered every captive and marched home in good order.

sentences.zh: 楊難敵自漢中還襲仇池，克之，執田崧，立之於前。

translations.literal: Yang Nan-di from Hanzhong returned raiding Chouci, overcame it, seized Tian Song, stood him before him.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Nan-di swept back from Hanzhong, stormed Chouci, seized Tian Song, and hauled him before his seat.

sentences.zh: 難敵左右叱崧令拜，崧瞋目叱之曰：「氐狗！

translations.literal: Nan-di’s left and right scolded Song ordering bow; Song glared eyes scolded them saying, “Di dogs!
translations.idiomatic: His guards ordered Tian Song to kneel. Tian Song glared and shouted, “Di dogs!

sentences.zh: 安有天子牧伯而向賊拜乎！

translations.literal: How is there Son of Heaven’s shepherd who bows toward bandits!
translations.idiomatic: Would an imperial governor kneel to rebels?

sentences.zh: 」難敵曰：「子岱，吾當與子終定大事。

translations.literal: ” Nan-di said, “Zi Dai, We ought with you finally settle great matters.
translations.idiomatic: ” Yang Nan-di said, “Zi Dai, you and I should finish the great work together.

sentences.zh: 子謂劉氏可為盡忠，吾獨不可乎！

translations.literal: You say Liu clan can be wholly loyal—are We alone unable!
translations.idiomatic: You think the Liu can be loyal—am I less able?

sentences.zh: 」崧厲色大言曰：「若賊氐奴才，安敢欲希覬非分！

translations.literal: ” Song stern color great speech said, “You bandit Di slave, how dare desire hope beyond allotment!
translations.idiomatic: ” Tian Song thundered, “You Di bandit, how dare you reach for what is not yours!

sentences.zh: 吾寧為國家鬼，豈可為汝臣，何不速殺我！

translations.literal: We rather be ghosts for the state—how can be your minister! Why not speed kill me!
translations.idiomatic: I would sooner haunt the Jin as a ghost than serve you—kill me now!

sentences.zh: 」顧排一人，取其劍，前刺難敵，不中，為難敵所殺。

translations.literal: ” He turned and shoved one man, took his sword, forward stabbed Nan-di, did not hit, was killed by Nan-di.
translations.idiomatic: ” He shouldered a guard aside, snatched his sword, and lunged at Yang Nan-di; missing, he was cut down.

sentences.zh: 曜遣劉岳攻石生於洛陽，配以近郡甲士五千，宿衛精卒一萬，濟自盟津。

translations.literal: Yao sent Liu Yue attack Shi Sheng at Luoyang, paired with near commandery armored soldiers five thousand, night-guard picked soldiers ten thousand, crossed from Meng Ford.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Yao dispatched Liu Yue against Shi Sheng in Luoyang with five thousand troops from neighboring commanderies and ten thousand picked guards, crossing at Meng Ford.

sentences.zh: 鎮東呼延謨率荊司之眾自崤澠而東。

translations.literal: Pacifier-of-the-East Huyan Mo led Jing and Si’s host from Xiao and Mian eastward.
translations.idiomatic: Huyan Mo, east-pacifying general, led the forces of Jing and Si east through the Xiao-Mian defiles.

sentences.zh: 岳攻石勒盟津、石梁二戍，克之，斬獲五千餘級，進圍石生於金墉。

translations.literal: Yue attacked Shi Le’s Meng Ford and Stone Beam two garrisons, overcame them, beheaded and captured five thousand-plus heads, advanced besieging Shi Sheng at Jinyong.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Yue took the Mengjin and Shiliang forts, killing or capturing over five thousand, and closed in on Shi Sheng at Jinyong.

sentences.zh: 石季龍率步騎四萬入自成皋關，岳陳兵以待之。

translations.literal: Shi Jilong led infantry and horse forty thousand entering through Chenggao Pass; Yue arrayed troops awaiting them.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Hu brought forty thousand horse and foot through Chenggao Pass; Liu Yao drew up his line to meet him.

sentences.zh: 戰于洛西，岳師敗績，岳中流矢，退保石梁。

translations.literal: They fought west of Luoyang; Yue’s army met crushing defeat; Yue was struck by a stray arrow and withdrew to hold Shiliang.
translations.idiomatic: West of Luoyang Liu Yue’s army was shattered; wounded by a stray shaft, he fell back to Shiliang.

sentences.zh: 季龍遂塹柵列圍，遏絕內外。

translations.literal: Jilong then ditched palisades and ringed the siege, cutting off inside and outside.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Hu threw up trenches and stockades, sealing the pocket.

sentences.zh: 岳眾饑甚，殺馬食之。

translations.literal: Yue’s host hungered severely, killed horses to eat them.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Yue’s men starved and butchered their horses for food.

sentences.zh: 季龍又敗呼延謨，斬之。

translations.literal: Jilong again defeated Huyan Mo, beheaded him.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Hu crushed Huyan Mo and took his head.

sentences.zh: 曜親率軍援岳，季龍率騎三萬來距。

translations.literal: Yao personally led the army to aid Yue; Jilong led thirty thousand horse to meet him.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Yao marched to relieve Liu Yue; Shi Hu opposed him with thirty thousand riders.

sentences.zh: 曜前軍劉黑大敗季龍將石聰於八特阪。

translations.literal: Yao’s vanguard Liu Hei greatly defeated Jilong’s general Shi Cong at Eight-Special Slope.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Hei, Liu Yao’s van commander, routed Shi Cong at Bate Slope.

sentences.zh: 曜次於金穀，夜無故大驚，軍中潰散，乃退如澠池。

translations.literal: Yao halted at Jingu; at night without cause great fright; the army scattered in panic; then withdrew toward Mianchi.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Yao camped at Jingu, but that night the host panicked without cause and melted away; he retreated toward Mianchi.

sentences.zh: 夜中又驚，士卒奔潰，遂歸長安。

translations.literal: In the night again frightened, soldiers fled in collapse; thereupon returned to Chang’an.
translations.idiomatic: The same terror struck the next night; the troops bolted, and Liu Yao fled all the way to Chang’an.

sentences.zh: 季龍執劉岳及其將王騰等八十餘人，並氐羌三千餘人，送于襄國，坑士卒一萬六千。

translations.literal: Jilong seized Liu Yue and his generals Wang Teng and others eighty-plus persons, together Di and Qiang three thousand-plus persons, sent them to Xiangguo, buried alive soldiers sixteen thousand.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Hu captured Liu Yue, Wang Teng, and more than eighty other officers, plus three thousand Di and Qiang auxiliaries, and sent them to Xiangguo; sixteen thousand common soldiers were buried alive.

sentences.zh: 曜至自澠池，素服郊哭，七日乃入城。

translations.literal: Yao arrived from Mianchi, in plain clothes wailed at the suburb seven days then entered the city.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Yao returned from Mianchi in undyed mourning, keened seven days outside the walls, then entered the capital.

sentences.zh: 武功豕生犬，上邽馬生牛，及諸妖變不可勝記。

translations.literal: Wugang swine bore dogs; Shanggui horses bore oxen; and various prodigies and anomalies beyond record.
translations.idiomatic: At Wugang sows whelped pups; at Shanggui mares dropped calves—monstrous signs too many to list.

sentences.zh: 曜命其公卿各舉博識直言之士一人，司马劉均舉參軍台產，曜親臨東堂，遣中黃門策問之。

translations.literal: Yao ordered his dukes and ministers each recommend one broadly learned straight-speaking gentleman; Minister Liu Jun recommended staff adviser Tai Chan; Yao personally attended the eastern hall and sent a palace eunuch to examine him by question.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Yao told every minister to nominate a learned, outspoken scholar; Liu Jun named Tai Chan. The emperor received him in the eastern hall and questioned him through a eunuch examiner.

sentences.zh: 產極言其故，曜覽而嘉之，引見東堂，訪以政事。

translations.literal: Chan spoke to the utmost the reasons; Yao read and praised him, led him in to the eastern hall, consulted him on government affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Tai Chan laid out the causes in full; Liu Yao, impressed, brought him into the eastern hall for policy talks.

sentences.zh: 產流涕歔欷，具陳災變之禍，政化之闕，辭旨諒直，曜改容禮之，即拜博士祭酒、諫議大夫，領太史令。

translations.literal: Chan wept and sobbed, fully set forth disaster-change’s harm, governance’s lacks; wording pointed and straight; Yao changed expression and honored him, immediately appointed him libationer of erudites, remonstrance grandee, concurrently grand astrologer.
translations.idiomatic: Weeping, Tai Chan detailed how omens spelled peril and where government failed. Liu Yao rose to honor him, naming him libationer of the academy, grandee of remonstrance, and director of astronomy.

sentences.zh: 其後所言皆驗，曜彌重之，歲中三遷，歷位尚書、光祿大夫、太子少師，位特進。

translations.literal: Afterward what he spoke all verified; Yao increasingly valued him; within the year thrice promoted, passing posts minister, grand master of golden seal, crown prince junior mentor, rank specially advanced.
translations.idiomatic: His forecasts came true; within a year Liu Yao promoted him thrice to minister, grand master of golden seal, junior tutor to the heir, and specially advanced noble.

sentences.zh: 曜署劉胤為大司馬，進封南陽王，以漢陽諸郡十三為國；

translations.literal: Yao appointed Liu Yin grand minister of war, advanced enfeoffment Prince of Nanyang, taking thirteen commanderies of Hanyang as his state;
translations.idiomatic: He made Liu Yin grand marshal and prince of Nanyang with a fief of thirteen Hanyang commanderies;

sentences.zh: 置單于台于渭城，拜大單于，置左右賢王已下，皆以胡、羯、鮮卑、氐、羌豪桀為之。

translations.literal: He set up the Chanyu terrace at Weicheng, invested the grand Chanyu, established left and right worthy kings downward, all using Hu, Jie, Xianbei, Di, Qiang chieftains for them.
translations.idiomatic: at Weicheng he built the Shanyu platform, took the title of supreme Shanyu, and named left and right “worthy kings” and other offices, filling them with Hu, Jie, Xianbei, Di, and Qiang chiefs.

sentences.zh: 曜自還長安，憤恚發病，至是疾瘳，曲赦長安殊死已下。

translations.literal: Yao since returning Chang’an, resentment and rage brought illness; reaching this illness healed; curved amnesty Chang’an short of capital death below.
translations.idiomatic: After his return to Chang’an, rage had sickened Liu Yao; now recovered, he proclaimed a limited amnesty in the capital.

sentences.zh: 署其汝南王劉咸為太尉、錄尚書事，光祿大夫劉綏為大司徒，卜泰為大司空。

translations.literal: He appointed his prince of Runan Liu Xian as grand commandant and recorder of secretariat affairs, grand master Liu Sui as grand minister over the masses, Bu Tai as minister of works.
translations.idiomatic: He named Liu Xian, prince of Runan, grand commandant and recorder of affairs; Liu Sui grand minister of education; Bu Tai minister of works.

sentences.zh: 曜妻劉氏疾甚，曜親省臨之，問其所欲言。

translations.literal: Yao’s wife Lady Liu was gravely ill; Yao personally visited and asked what she wished to say.
translations.idiomatic: Lady Liu, the empress, lay dying; Liu Yao attended her bedside and asked her last requests.

sentences.zh: 劉泣曰：「妾叔父昶無子，妾少養于叔，恩撫甚隆，無以報德，願陛下貴之。

translations.literal: Liu wept saying, “My uncle Chang has no sons; I was reared young by uncle, kindness and care very abundant; no means to repay virtue; wish Your Majesty honor him.
translations.idiomatic: Weeping, she said, “My uncle Liu Chang has no heir; he raised me with overflowing kindness. I cannot repay him—please honor him, sire.

sentences.zh: 妾叔皚女芳有德色，願備後宮。

translations.literal: My uncle Ai’s daughter Fang has virtuous beauty; wish to prepare rear palace.
translations.idiomatic: His daughter Fang, my cousin, is virtuous and lovely—take her into the harem.”

sentences.zh: 」曜許之。

translations.literal: ” Yao granted it.
translations.idiomatic: ” Liu Yao consented.

sentences.zh: 言終而死，偽諡獻烈皇后。

translations.literal: When her words ended she died, falsely posthumous titled Empress Xianlie.
translations.idiomatic: She died as she finished; he gave her the posthumous name Empress Xianlie.

sentences.zh: 以劉昶為使持節、侍中、大司徒、錄尚書事，進封河南郡公，封昶妻張氏為慈鄉君，立劉皚女芳為皇后，追念劉氏之言也。

translations.literal: He made Liu Chang credential bearer, palace attendant, grand minister over the masses, recorder of secretariat affairs, advanced enfeoffment Duke of Henan commandery, enfeoffed Chang’s wife Lady Zhang as lady of Cixiang, established Liu Ai’s daughter Fang as empress, remembering Lady Liu’s words.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Chang became credential bearer, palace attendant, grand minister of education, and duke of Henan; Lady Zhang was lady of Cixiang; Fang was made empress to fulfill the dying empress’s plea.

sentences.zh: 俄署驃騎劉述為大司徒，劉昶為太保。

translations.literal: Soon he appointed swift-cavalry Liu Shu grand minister over the masses, Liu Chang grand guardian.
translations.idiomatic: Soon Liu Shu replaced him as grand minister of education while Liu Chang became grand guardian.

sentences.zh: 召公卿已下子弟有勇幹者為親禦郎，被甲乘鎧馬，動止自隨，以充折沖之任。

translations.literal: He summoned dukes and ministers’ sons and younger brothers who had courage and capacity to be personal guard gentlemen, armored riding armored horses, moving and halting following him, to fill the duty of breaking shock.
translations.idiomatic: Sons of officials with martial talent were enrolled as imperial guardsmen in armor on barded horses, attending Liu Yao everywhere as a crack corps.

sentences.zh: 尚書郝述、都水使者支當等固諫，曜大怒，鴆而殺之。

translations.literal: Minister Hao Shu, waterworks commissioner Zhi Dang and others firmly remonstrated; Yao greatly angry, poisoned and killed them.
translations.idiomatic: Hao Shu, Zhi Dang, and others protested; Liu Yao, furious, had them poisoned.

sentences.zh: 咸和三年，夜夢三人金面丹脣，東向逡巡，不言而退，曜拜而履其跡。

translations.literal: Third year of Xianhe, at night he dreamed three men gold-faced cinnabar lips, eastward hesitating, not speaking then withdrew; Yao bowed and trod their footprints.
translations.idiomatic: In the third Xianhe year Liu Yao dreamed of three golden-faced, vermilion-lipped figures pacing east in silence, then retreating; he bowed and stepped in their tracks.

sentences.zh: 旦召公卿已下議之，朝臣咸賀以為吉祥，惟太史令任義進曰：「三者，曆運統之極也。

translations.literal: At dawn he summoned dukes and ministers downward to deliberate; court ministers all congratulated deeming it auspicious; only grand astrologer Ren Yi advanced saying, “Three is the extreme of calendar-fate’s succession.
translations.idiomatic: At dawn he asked his court; all hailed it as lucky save Grand Astrologer Ren Yi, who said, “Three marks the limit of a heavenly mandate.

sentences.zh: 東為震位，王者之始次也。

translations.literal: East is the Zhen position, the king’s beginning next.
translations.idiomatic: East is the Zhen trigram—the first station of kingship.

sentences.zh: 金為兌位，物衰落也。

translations.literal: Metal is the Dui position, things decline and fall.
translations.idiomatic: Metal is Dui—the phase of decay.

sentences.zh: 脣丹不言，事之畢也。

translations.literal: Cinnabar lips not speaking means affairs concluded.
translations.idiomatic: Red lips sealed mean the matter is finished.

sentences.zh: 逡巡揖讓，退舍之道也。

translations.literal: Hesitating yielding and deferring is the way of retreating and yielding.
translations.idiomatic: Hesitant courtesy is the etiquette of yielding ground.

sentences.zh: 為之拜者，屈伏於人也。

translations.literal: For him to bow means bent submission to others.
translations.idiomatic: Your bow shows you yielding to another.

sentences.zh: 履跡而行，慎不出疆也。

translations.literal: Treading footprints and walking means careful not to cross borders.
translations.idiomatic: Walking in their steps warns you not to overstep your realm.

sentences.zh: 東井，秦分也。

translations.literal: Eastern Well is Qin’s division.
translations.idiomatic: The Eastern Well asterism governs Qin.

sentences.zh: 五車，趙分也。

translations.literal: Five Chariots is Zhao’s division.
translations.idiomatic: The Five Chariots govern Zhao.

sentences.zh: 秦兵必暴起，亡主喪師，留敗趙地。

translations.literal: Qin’s armies will suddenly rise, lose the lord and ruin the army, stay defeated in Zhao’s territory.
translations.idiomatic: Qin’s hosts will strike: the sovereign will fall, the army perish, and Zhao’s soil will know defeat.

sentences.zh: 遠至三年，近七百日，其應不遠。

translations.literal: Far reaches three years, near seven hundred days—the response is not distant.
translations.idiomatic: At farthest three years, at nearest seven hundred days—the reckoning draws near.

sentences.zh: 願陛下思而防之。

translations.literal: Wish Your Majesty ponder and guard against it.
translations.idiomatic: I beg you to reflect and prepare.”

sentences.zh: 」曜大懼，於是躬親二郊，飾繕神祠，望秩山川，靡不周及。

translations.literal: ” Yao greatly feared; thereupon personally attended the two suburban altars, adorned and repaired spirit shrines, offered ranked sacrifice to mountains and rivers, none not thoroughly reached.
translations.idiomatic: ” Liu Yao was terrified. He personally worshipped at the suburban altars, refurbished every shrine, and sacrificed to mountains and rivers without omission.

sentences.zh: 大赦殊死已下，復百姓租稅之半。

translations.literal: Great amnesty short of capital death below, restored commoners’ rent and tax by half.
translations.idiomatic: He offered a general amnesty short of capital crimes and halved the people’s taxes.

sentences.zh: 長安自春不雨，至於五月。

translations.literal: Chang’an from spring did not rain until fifth month.
translations.idiomatic: No rain fell on Chang’an from spring until the fifth month.

sentences.zh: 曜遣其武衛劉朗率騎三萬襲楊難敵于仇池，弗克，掠三千餘戶而歸。

translations.literal: Yao sent his martial guard Liu Lang leading thirty thousand horse to raid Yang Nan-di at Chouci, did not overcome, plundered three thousand-plus households and returned.
translations.idiomatic: He sent Liu Lang with thirty thousand riders against Yang Nan-di at Chouci; failing to win, Liu Lang seized three thousand households and withdrew.

sentences.zh: 張駿聞曜軍為石氐所敗，乃去曜官號，復稱晉大將軍、涼州牧，遣金城太守張閬及枹罕護軍辛晏、將軍韓璞等率眾數萬人，自大夏攻掠秦州諸郡。

translations.literal: Zhang Jun heard Yao’s army was by Shi clan defeated, then removed Yao’s official titles, again called himself Jin grand general, Liangzhou shepherd, sent Jincheng administrator Zhang Lang and Fuhan protector Xin Yan, general Han Pu and others leading host several tens of thousands, from Daxia raiding Qinzhou’s various commanderies.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhang Jun learned Liu Yao had lost to the Shi, he dropped Zhao’s titles, resumed the Jin rank of grand general and governor of Liang, and sent Zhang Lang, Xin Yan, Han Pu, and tens of thousands from Daxia to raid Qinzhou.

sentences.zh: 曜遣劉胤率步騎四萬擊之，夾洮相持七十餘日。

translations.literal: Yao sent Liu Yin leading infantry and horse forty thousand to strike them, flanking the Tao and facing each other seventy-plus days.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Yao countered with forty thousand men under Liu Yin; the armies glared at each other across the Tao for seventy days.

sentences.zh: 冠軍呼延那雞率親禦郎二千騎，絕其運路。

translations.literal: Champion Huyan Naji led personal guard gentlemen two thousand horse, cut their transport road.
translations.idiomatic: Huyan Naji, champion general, took two thousand imperial guards and severed the enemy supply line.

sentences.zh: 胤濟師逼之，璞軍大潰，奔還涼州。

translations.literal: Yin crossed troops pressing them; Pu’s army greatly collapsed, fled back to Liangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Yin forced the crossing; Han Pu’s line broke and fled to Liangzhou.

sentences.zh: 胤追之，及于令居，斬級二萬。

translations.literal: Yin pursued them, caught them at Lingju, beheaded twenty thousand heads.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Yin overtook them at Lingju and took twenty thousand heads.

sentences.zh: 張閬、辛晏率眾數萬降於曜，皆拜將軍，封列侯。

translations.literal: Zhang Lang, Xin Yan led host several tens of thousands submitted to Yao, all appointed generals, enfeoffed full marquises.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Lang and Xin Yan surrendered tens of thousands; Liu Yao made them generals and full marquises.

sentences.zh: 石勒遣石季龍率眾四萬，自軹關西入伐曜，河東應之者五十餘縣，進攻蒲阪。

translations.literal: Shi Le sent Shi Jilong leading host forty thousand, from Zhiguan west entering to campaign against Yao; Hedong responded fifty-plus counties, advanced attacking Puban.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Le dispatched Shi Hu with forty thousand men west through Zhiguan against Liu Yao; more than fifty Hedong counties rose in support as the column advanced on Puban.

sentences.zh: 曜將東救蒲阪，懼張駿、楊難敵承虛襲長安，遣其河間王述發氐羌之眾屯于秦州。

translations.literal: Yao was about east to rescue Puban, feared Zhang Jun, Yang Nan-di would take void to raid Chang’an, sent his Prince of Hejian Shu to mobilize Di and Qiang host and encamp at Qinzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Yao meant to relieve Puban but feared Zhang Jun and Yang Nan-di would strike an empty Chang’an, so he ordered Prince Liu Shu of Hejian to rally Di and Qiang troops on Qinzhou.

sentences.zh: 曜盡中外精銳水陸赴之，自衛關北濟。

translations.literal: Yao exhausted inner and outer picked keen by water and land to hasten there, from Weiguan north crossed.
translations.idiomatic: He threw every elite by river and road into the march, crossing north from Weiguan.

sentences.zh: 季龍懼，引師而退。

translations.literal: Jilong feared, led army and withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Hu pulled back in alarm.

sentences.zh: 追之，及于高候，大戰，敗之，斬其將軍石瞻，枕屍二百餘里，收其資仗億計。

translations.literal: They pursued, caught them at Gaohou, great battle, defeated them, beheaded their general Shi Zhan, corpses pillow two hundred-plus li, gathered their gear and arms beyond reckoning.
translations.idiomatic: They overtook him at Gaohou, shattered his army, killed Shi Zhan, and left corpses stacked for two hundred li, seizing immeasurable arms and baggage.

sentences.zh: 季龍奔於朝歌。

translations.literal: Jilong fled to Zhaoge.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Hu fled to Zhaoge.

sentences.zh: 曜遂濟自大陽，攻石生於金墉，決千金堨以灌之。

translations.literal: Yao then crossed from Dayang, attacked Shi Sheng at Jinyong, breached the Qianjin weir to flood him.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Yao crossed at Dayang, besieged Shi Sheng at Jinyong, and broke the Qianjin dike to flood the walls.

sentences.zh: 曜不撫士眾，專與嬖臣飲博，左右或諫，曜怒，以為妖言，斬之。

translations.literal: Yao did not comfort soldiers and host, solely with favorite ministers drank and gambled; left and right some remonstrated; Yao angry, deemed it inauspicious speech, beheaded them.
translations.idiomatic: He ignored the troops, drinking and dicing with favorites; anyone who remonstrated he called a bearer of ill omen and executed.

sentences.zh: 大風拔樹，昏霧四塞。

translations.literal: Great wind uprooted trees; dim fog blocked four sides.
translations.idiomatic: Gales tore up trees and fog choked the field.

sentences.zh: 聞季龍進據石門，續知勒自率大眾已濟，始議增滎陽戍，杜黃馬關。

translations.literal: He heard Jilong advanced and held Stone Gate; soon knew Le personally led great host already crossed; only then deliberated increasing Yingyang garrison, blocking Huangma Pass.
translations.idiomatic: Learning that Shi Hu held Shimen and that Shi Le himself had crossed the river with the main army, he belatedly ordered reinforcements for Yingyang and sealed Huangma Pass.

sentences.zh: 俄而洛水候者與勒前鋒交戰，擒羯，送之。

translations.literal: Soon Luoshui scouts battled Le’s vanguard, captured a Jie, sent him.
translations.idiomatic: Scouts on the Luo clashed with Shi Le’s van, took a Jie prisoner, and brought him in.

sentences.zh: 曜問曰：「大胡自來邪？

translations.literal: Yao asked, “Did the great Hu come himself?
translations.idiomatic: Liu Yao asked, “Has the great Khan come in person?

sentences.zh: 其眾大小復如何？

translations.literal: How are his hosts large and small?
translations.idiomatic: How large is his force?

sentences.zh: 」羯曰：「大胡自來，軍盛不可當也。

translations.literal: ” The Jie said, “The great Hu came himself; the army’s splendor cannot be withstood.
translations.idiomatic: ” The prisoner said, “He leads in person, and his host is irresistible.”

sentences.zh: 」曜色變，使攝金墉之圍，陳於洛西，南北十餘里。

translations.literal: ” Yao’s color changed; he ordered lift the Jinyong siege and array west of the Luo, north–south ten-plus li.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Yao paled, raised the siege of Jinyong, and drew up a line ten li along the western bank.

sentences.zh: 曜少而淫酒，末年尤甚。

translations.literal: From youth Yao was dissolute in wine; in later years especially severe.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Yao had been a drunkard since youth; in old age it was worse.

sentences.zh: 勒至，曜將戰，飲酒數斗，常乘赤馬無故局頓，乃乘小馬。

translations.literal: When Le arrived, Yao was about to fight, drank several dou of wine; always rode a red horse that for no reason stumbled, then rode a small horse.
translations.idiomatic: On the day of battle he quaffed several dou before riding out; his red mount kept stumbling, so he switched to a pony.

sentences.zh: 比出，復飲酒鬥餘。

translations.literal: By the time he went out, again drank more than a dou of wine.
translations.idiomatic: He swallowed another dou on the way to the field.

sentences.zh: 至於西陽門，捴陣就平，勒將石堪因而乘之，師遂大潰。

translations.literal: Reaching Xiyang Gate, he drew the line onto level ground; Le’s general Shi Kan seized the moment and struck; the army thereupon greatly collapsed.
translations.idiomatic: At the Xiyang Gate he moved onto open ground; Shi Kan, Shi Le’s general, charged the formation and broke it utterly.

sentences.zh: 曜昏醉奔退，馬陷石渠，墜於冰上，被瘡十餘，通中者三，為堪所執，送於勒所。

translations.literal: Yao, muddled drunk, fled retreating; horse sank in a stone ditch, fell on ice, suffered more than ten wounds, three piercing through; was seized by Kan, sent to Le’s place.
translations.idiomatic: Reeling drunk, Liu Yao fled until his horse foundered in a stone channel on the ice; a dozen wounds, three mortal, brought him down into Shi Kan’s hands and before Shi Le.

sentences.zh: 曜曰：「石王！

translations.literal: Yao said, “King Shi!
translations.idiomatic: Liu Yao cried, “King Shi!

sentences.zh: 憶重門之盟不？

translations.literal: Do you recall the covenant at Chongmen?
translations.idiomatic: Do you remember our oath at Chongmen?

sentences.zh: 」勒使徐光謂曜曰：「今日之事，天使其然，復云何邪！

translations.literal: ” Le ordered Xu Guang to tell Yao, “Today’s affair—Heaven made it thus; what more is there to say!
translations.idiomatic: ” Shi Le had Xu Guang answer, “Today heaven decreed this—what use in talk?”

sentences.zh: 」幽曜于河南丞廨，使金瘡醫李永療之，歸於襄國。

translations.literal: ” He imprisoned Yao in the Henan assistant’s yamen, had wound physician Li Yong treat him, returned him to Xiangguo.
translations.idiomatic: ” He jailed Liu Yao in the Henan clerk’s compound, had the surgeon Li Yong bind his wounds, then sent him to Xiangguo.

sentences.zh: 曜瘡甚，勒載以馬輿，使李永與同載。

translations.literal: Yao’s wounds were severe; Le carried him in a horse-litter, ordered Li Yong ride with him.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Yao’s wounds festered; Shi Le carried him in a litter and seated Li Yong beside him.

sentences.zh: 北苑市三老孫機上禮求見曜，勒許之。

translations.literal: Three elders of the North Park market, Sun Ji, submitted rites asking to see Yao; Le granted it.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Ji, an elder of the north market, begged an audience; Shi Le allowed it.

sentences.zh: 機進酒於曜曰：「僕谷王，關右稱帝皇。

translations.literal: Ji advanced wine to Yao saying, “Bugu king, west of the passes hailed emperor.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Ji raised a cup: “The Bugu king west of the passes was hailed as emperor.

sentences.zh: 當持重，保土疆。

translations.literal: You should have held steady and guarded the soil.
translations.idiomatic: He should have held his ground and kept his borders.

sentences.zh: 輕用兵，敗洛陽。

translations.literal: Lightly used arms—lost Luoyang.
translations.idiomatic: He squandered his armies and lost Luoyang.

sentences.zh: 祚運窮，天所亡。

translations.literal: Fortune’s luck exhausted—Heaven destroyed him.
translations.idiomatic: Heaven ended his mandate.

sentences.zh: 開大分，持一觴。

translations.literal: Now the great divide opens—take this cup.
translations.idiomatic: The end is plain—drink this cup.”

sentences.zh: 」曜曰：「何以健邪！

translations.literal: ” Yao said, “How hearty!
translations.idiomatic: ” Liu Yao said, “Well sung!

sentences.zh: 當為翁飲。

translations.literal: Let me drink for the old man.
translations.idiomatic: I will drink with you, elder.”

sentences.zh: 」勒聞之，淒然改容曰：「亡國之人，足令老叟數之。

translations.literal: ” Le heard it, mournfully changed expression saying, “A ruined state’s man is enough to make an old fellow count his faults.
translations.idiomatic: ” Shi Le listened, face tightening: “A fallen sovereign lets an old man reckon his sins.

sentences.zh: 」舍曜于襄國永豐小城，給其妓妾，嚴兵圍守。

translations.literal: ” He housed Yao in Yongfeng lesser city at Xiangguo, supplied him singing-girls and concubines, strict troops ring-guarded.
translations.idiomatic: ” He lodged Liu Yao in the small Yongfeng compound at Xiangguo with entertainers but ringed him with guards.

sentences.zh: 遣劉岳、劉震等乘馬，從男女，衣㡊以見曜，曜曰：「久謂卿等為灰土，石王仁厚，全宥至今，而我殺石他，負盟之甚。

translations.literal: He sent Liu Yue, Liu Zhen and others riding horses, following men and women, wearing gauze caps to see Yao; Yao said, “Long I thought you were ash and earth; King Shi’s kindness spared you until now, yet I killed Shi Ta—how deep the breach of our pact.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Yue and Liu Zhen rode in, disguised in soft caps with their households. Liu Yao said, “I had given you up for dead; King Shi’s mercy kept you alive while I slew Shi Ta—my treachery was great.

sentences.zh: 今日之禍，自其分耳。

translations.literal: Today’s disaster is my own portion.
translations.idiomatic: This ruin is my desert.”

sentences.zh: 」留宴終日而去。

translations.literal: ” He kept them feasting all day then departed.
translations.idiomatic: ” They feasted the day through and left.

sentences.zh: 勒諭曜與其太子熙書，令速降之，曜但敕熙：「與諸大臣匡維社稷，勿以吾易意也。

translations.literal: Le instructed Yao to write his heir Xi a letter ordering quick surrender; Yao only instructed Xi, “With the great ministers uphold the altars; do not change course because of me.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Le told him to order Crown Prince Xi to yield; Liu Yao wrote only, “Stand with your ministers for the state; do not shift policy on my account.

sentences.zh: 」勒覽而惡之，後為勒所殺。

translations.literal: ” Le read and hated it; afterward Yao was killed by Le.
translations.idiomatic: ” Shi Le, reading this, had him murdered.

sentences.zh: 熙及劉胤、劉咸等議西保秦州，尚書胡勳曰：「今雖喪主，國尚全完，將士情一，未有離叛，可共並力距險，走未晚也。

translations.literal: Xi together with Liu Yin, Liu Xian and others deliberated fleeing west to hold Qinzhou; Minister Hu Xun said, “Though we have lost the lord, the state is still whole, generals and soldiers of one mind, none yet rebel—together we can hold the defiles; flight is not yet timely.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Xi, Liu Yin, and Liu Xian planned to withdraw to Qinzhou. Hu Xun urged, “The emperor is gone but the realm holds, morale is firm—hold the passes together before you run.”

sentences.zh: 」胤不從，怒其沮眾，斬之，遂率百官奔於上邽，劉厚、劉策皆捐鎮奔之。

translations.literal: ” Yin did not follow, angry that he dampened the host, beheaded him, then led the hundred officials fleeing to Shanggui; Liu Hou, Liu Ce both abandoned posts and ran to them.
translations.idiomatic: ” Liu Yin refused, executed him for cowing the troops, and fled to Shanggui with the court; Liu Hou and Liu Ce abandoned their commands to join him.

sentences.zh: 關中擾亂，將軍蔣英、辛恕擁眾數十萬，據長安，遣使招勒，勒遣石生率洛陽之眾以赴之。

translations.literal: Guanzhong was in turmoil; generals Jiang Ying, Xin Shu held several hundred thousand, occupied Chang’an, sent envoys summoning Le; Le sent Shi Sheng leading Luoyang’s host to answer them.
translations.idiomatic: Generals Jiang Ying and Xin Shu seized Chang’an with a huge force and invited Shi Le, who sent Shi Sheng from Luoyang.

sentences.zh: 胤及劉遵率眾數萬，自上邽將攻石生於長安，隴東、武都、安定、新平、北地、扶風、始平諸郡戎夏皆起兵應胤。

translations.literal: Yin and Liu Zun led several tens of thousands from Shanggui to attack Shi Sheng at Chang’an; Longdong, Wudu, Anding, Xinping, Beidi, Fufeng, Shi Ping commanderies, Rong and Xia, all raised troops answering Yin.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Yin and Liu Zun marched from Shanggui on Shi Sheng; every county from Longdong to Fufeng rose for them.

sentences.zh: 胤次於仲橋，石生固守長安。

translations.literal: Yin halted at Zhongqiao; Shi Sheng stubbornly held Chang’an.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Yin camped at Zhongqiao while Shi Sheng held fast in Chang’an.

sentences.zh: 勒使石季龍率騎二萬距胤，戰于義渠，為季龍所敗，死者五千餘人。

translations.literal: Le ordered Shi Jilong to lead twenty thousand horse to oppose Yin; they fought at Yiqu; Yin was by Jilong defeated, dead five thousand-plus.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Hu met him at Yiqu with twenty thousand riders and broke him, leaving five thousand dead.

sentences.zh: 胤奔上邽，季龍乘勝追戰，枕屍千里，上邽潰。

translations.literal: Yin fled to Shanggui; Jilong rode victory pursuing battle, corpses pillow a thousand li, Shanggui collapsed.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Yin raced back to Shanggui; Shi Hu chased him a thousand li of carnage and stormed the city.

sentences.zh: 季龍執其偽太子熙、南陽王劉胤並將相諸王等及其諸卿校公侯已下三千餘人，皆殺之。

translations.literal: Jilong seized false heir Xi, Prince of Nanyang Liu Yin together with generals, ministers, various kings and their ministers, colonels, dukes, marquises downward three thousand-plus persons, all killed them.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Hu took the pretender Liu Xi, Prince Liu Yin of Nanyang, and three thousand nobles and officers and put them all to the sword.

sentences.zh: 徙其台省文武、關東流人、秦雍大族九千餘人于襄國，又坑其王公等及五郡屠各五千餘人於洛陽。

translations.literal: He moved their terrace and ministry civil and military, Guandong exiles, Qin-Yong great clans nine thousand-plus persons to Xiangguo, again buried alive their princes and dukes and five-commandery Tuge five thousand-plus persons at Luoyang.
translations.idiomatic: Nine thousand officials, eastern refugees, and great clans were shipped to Xiangguo; five thousand Tuge nobles were buried alive at Luoyang.

sentences.zh: 曜在位十年而敗。

translations.literal: Yao was on the throne ten years then defeated.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Yao reigned ten years before ruin.

sentences.zh: 始，元海以懷帝永嘉四年僭位，至曜三世，凡二十有七載，以成帝咸和四年滅。

translations.literal: At first Yuanhai at Emperor Huai’s Yongjia fourth year usurped the throne; reaching Yao three generations, altogether twenty-seven years, perished in Emperor Cheng’s Xianhe fourth year.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Yuan had seized the throne in Yongjia 4 of Emperor Huai; three generations and twenty-seven years later Zhao fell in Xianhe 4 of Emperor Cheng.

sentences.zh: 【史評】

translations.literal: 【Historical appraisal】
translations.idiomatic: Historians’ commentary

sentences.zh: 史臣曰：彼戎狄者，人面獸心，見利則棄君親，臨財則忘仁義者也。

translations.literal: The historians say: Those Rong and Di have human faces and beast hearts; seeing profit they cast aside lord and kin; facing wealth they forget benevolence and right.
translations.idiomatic: The historians wrote: The northern tribes wear human faces but beastly hearts—they forsake sovereign and family for gain and trample duty for gold.

sentences.zh: 投之遐遠，猶懼外侵，而處以封畿，窺我中釁。

translations.literal: Cast them far away, still fear outward invasion; yet seat them within the royal domain, they spy our central troubles.
translations.idiomatic: Banish them and they still threaten the frontier; nest them in the heartland and they watch for weakness.

sentences.zh: 昔者幽-{后}-不綱，胡塵暗于戲水；

translations.literal: In old days Queen You lost the reins, Hu dust darkened the waters at Yi;
translations.idiomatic: When Queen Bao Si unraveled the Zhou, barbarian dust dimmed the Yi River;

sentences.zh: 襄王失御，戎馬生於關洛。

translations.literal: King Xiang lost the chariot-reins, war-horses foaled at Guan and Luo.
translations.idiomatic: when King Xiang lost control, war-horses bred within Guan and Luo.

sentences.zh: 至於算強弱，妙兵權，體興衰，知利害，于我中華未可量也。

translations.literal: As to reckoning strength and weakness, mastering stratagem, reading rise and fall, knowing gain and harm—toward our Hua Xia they cannot be measured.
translations.idiomatic: Yet in gauging power, wielding arms, and reading fortune they are not to be despised.

sentences.zh: 況元海人傑，必致青雲之上；

translations.literal: How much more Yuanhai a human prodigy, sure to reach above the blue clouds;
translations.idiomatic: Liu Yuan was a prodigy born to rise;

sentences.zh: 許以殊才，不居庸劣之下。

translations.literal: granted unusual talent, he would not stay beneath the mediocre.
translations.idiomatic: given rare gifts, he would not languish among the mean.

sentences.zh: 是以策馬鴻騫，乘機豹變，五部高嘯，一旦推雄，皇枝相害，未有與之爭衡者矣。

translations.literal: Therefore he spurred his horse like a wild swan, seized the moment like a leopard’s change; the five divisions howled high; in one morning he thrust himself forward as champion; imperial branches slew one another—none could vie with him.
translations.idiomatic: So he rode the tide like a soaring goose, transformed like the leopard in the Book of Changes; the five Xiongnu camps roared him to the fore while Jin princes cut one another down—none could match him.

sentences.zh: 伊秩啟興王之略，骨都論克定之秋，單于無北顧之懷，獫狁有南郊之祭，大哉天地，茲為不仁矣！

translations.literal: Yizhi opened the plan of a rising king, Gudu debated the season to conquer and settle; the Shanyu had no thought of glancing north; the Xianyun held sacrifice at the southern suburb—great indeed are Heaven and Earth; this was unkindness!
translations.idiomatic: Ministers plotted founding rites, chiefs argued the hour of conquest; the Shanyu faced south while former foes offered suburban sacrifice—how vast heaven and earth, and how pitiless the turn!

sentences.zh: 若乃習以華風，溫乎雅度；

translations.literal: If they practiced Chinese ways, warmed in cultured demeanor;
translations.idiomatic: Those who took up Chinese polish and mild manners

sentences.zh: 兼其舊俗，則罕規模。

translations.literal: mixed with their old customs, then rarely matched the model.
translations.idiomatic: yet clung to steppe habit seldom matched the civil ideal.

sentences.zh: 雖復石勒稱籓，王彌效款，終為夷狄之邦，未辯君臣之位。

translations.literal: Though again Shi Le declared vassalage, Wang Mi showed sincerity, in the end they remained barbarian states, not clarifying the relation of lord and minister.
translations.idiomatic: Even when Shi Le bowed as vassal and Wang Mi pledged fealty, they stayed alien realms without true ministerial order.

sentences.zh: 至於不遠儒風，虛襟正直，則昔賢所謂並仁義而盜之者焉。

translations.literal: As for not spurning Confucian ways, emptying the breast toward integrity—this is what past worthies called stealing even while wielding benevolence and right.
translations.idiomatic: Those who feigned Confucian respect while grasping power were, as sages said, robbers cloaked in virtue.

sentences.zh: 偽主斯亡，玄明篡嗣，樹恩戎旅，既總威權，關河開曩日之疆，士馬倍前人之氣。

translations.literal: When the false sovereign perished, Xuanming seized the succession, planted favor in the armies, and once he held full might, the passes and rivers opened old frontiers and men and horses doubled their former pride.
translations.idiomatic: When Liu Cong died, Liu Yao seized the line, curried the camps, and commanded such power that the old Qin-Jin borders reopened and his host doubled in arrogance.

sentences.zh: 然則信不由中，自乖弘遠，貌之為美，處事難終。

translations.literal: Yet trust did not come from within; he contradicted his own breadth; the face of virtue masked deeds hard to finish.
translations.idiomatic: Yet his faith was hollow, his vision narrow; fair show could not carry policy through.

sentences.zh: 縱武窮兵，殘忠害謇，佞人方轡，並-{后}-載馳，閹豎類於回天，凝科逾於砲烙。

translations.literal: He exhausted force in war, maimed the loyal, silenced the blunt; sycophants rode paired reins, consorts galloped beside him; eunuchs seemed to turn heaven, cruel law outdid the roasting pillar.
translations.idiomatic: He waged war to the limit, struck down honest men, and paired flatterers with favorites while eunuchs twisted the court and punishments grew crueler than the Shang’s bronze.

sentences.zh: 遣豺狼之將，逐鷹犬之師，懸旌俯渭，分麾陷洛，鐵馬陵山，胡笳遵渚，粉忠貞於戎手，聚搢紳於京觀。

translations.literal: He sent wolf-like generals and hawkish hosts; banners hung over the Wei, staffs divided to take Luoyang; armored horses scaled hills, Hu pipes sounded along islets; he ground loyalty in barbarian hands and heaped gentry in victory mounds.
translations.idiomatic: Wolfish captains and houndlike columns swept the Wei, stormed Luoyang, trampled hills, and wailed on the rivers—loyalists crushed, scholars piled in corpse mounds.

sentences.zh: 先王井賦，乃眷維桑；

translations.literal: The former kings’ well-and-field levies—thus they cherished the mulberry at home;
translations.idiomatic: The ancient well-tax fields became the mulberry lanes they loved;

sentences.zh: 舊都宮室，咸成茂草。

translations.literal: the old capital’s palaces all turned rank grass.
translations.idiomatic: the old capitals sank under wild grass.

sentences.zh: 墜露沾衣，行人灑淚。

translations.literal: Dew dripping soaked travelers’ clothes; wayfarers sprinkled tears.
translations.idiomatic: Dew soaked the traveler’s sleeve; every passerby wept.

sentences.zh: 若乃上古敦龐，不親其子，功成高讓，歸諸有德。

translations.literal: As for high antiquity’s honest simplicity, not doting on sons, merit done and loftily yielding, handing all to the worthy—
translations.idiomatic: In high antiquity fathers did not coddle sons; merit won, they yielded to worthies—

sentences.zh: 爰及三伐，乃用干戈，將以拯厥版蕩，恭膺天命。

translations.literal: coming to the three campaigns, then arms were used, intending to rescue that overturning turmoil, reverently bearing Heaven’s mandate.
translations.idiomatic: later ages took up arms to save chaos and answer heaven’s charge.

sentences.zh: 懿彼武王，殷之列辟，載旆乘時，興兵誓野，投焚既隕，可以絕言。

translations.literal: Ah, King Wu, Yin’s feudal lord—he raised banners, seized the hour, swore oaths in the wilds; once the pyre fell, speech could end.
translations.idiomatic: King Wu of Zhou, vassal of Shang, marched with banners and oaths; when the fires of Yin died, judgment was sealed.

sentences.zh: 而輕呂旁揮，彤弧三發，豈若響清蹕于常道之門，馳金車于山陽之館！

translations.literal: Yet lightly he swung the Qinglü blade, thrice drew the crimson bow—how does that compare to hearing clear convoys at Changdao Gate, driving the gold chariot to Shanyang lodge!
translations.idiomatic: Yet he swung the Qinglü halberd and shot thrice with the red bow—nothing like the solemn convoys at Changdao or the golden coach at Shanyang!

sentences.zh: 故知黔首來蘇，居今愛古；

translations.literal: Thus know the black-haired masses welcome renewal—they love the present and honor the past;
translations.idiomatic: The people welcome renewal and cherish old virtue;

sentences.zh: 白旗陳肆，古不如今。

translations.literal: white flags in the market—antiquity cannot match today’s shame.
translations.idiomatic: yet white flags in the square show today’s shame outdoes antiquity.

sentences.zh: 胡寇不仁，有同豺豕，役天子以行觴，驅乘輿以執蓋，庾瑉之淚既盡，辛賓加之以血。

translations.literal: The Hu bandits were unkind, the same as wolves and swine; they made the Son of Heaven pour their cups, drove the imperial carriage to hold their canopies; Yu Min’s tears ran dry, Xin Bin’s blood was added.
translations.idiomatic: Those Hu were beasts: they poured wine for captive emperors, made imperial carriages shade their feasts; Yu Min wept himself dry, Xin Bin bled for it.

sentences.zh: 若乃有生之貴，處死為難，弘在三之義，忘七尺之重，主憂之恨，畢命同歸，自古篡奪，於斯為甚。

translations.literal: As for holding life precious yet facing death as hard, enlarging the threefold devotion, forgetting the seven-foot frame—hatred for the lord’s sorrow, giving life on the same pyre—never in usurpation was it worse.
translations.idiomatic: To prize life yet choose death for the threefold bonds, scorning mere flesh—dying with a grieving lord—never was usurpation crueller.

sentences.zh: 是以災氣呈形，賊臣苞亂，政荒民散，可以危亡。

translations.literal: Therefore baleful qi showed shapes, traitorous ministers wrapped chaos; government wasted, people scattered—thus ruin came.
translations.idiomatic: So omens took form, rebels bred, rule failed and folk fled—ruin followed.

sentences.zh: 劉聰竟得壽終，非不幸也。

translations.literal: Liu Cong yet got to die in his bed—not unlucky.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Cong died in his bed—hardly the worst fate.

sentences.zh: 曜則天資虓勇，運偶時艱，用兵則王翦之倫，好殺亦董公之亞。

translations.literal: Yao was by nature fierce and brave, his lot cast in hard times; in war he ranked with Wang Jian, in love of killing he stood second to Duke Dong.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Yao was savage by nature, soldier in an evil age—general like Wang Jian, slaughterer near Dong Zhuo’s ilk.

sentences.zh: 而承基丑類，或有可稱。

translations.literal: Yet inheriting base stock, still something could be praised.
translations.idiomatic: Yet rising from a flawed house, he had his merits.

sentences.zh: 子遠納忠，高旌暫偃；

translations.literal: Ziyuan accepted loyalty—the high banner briefly furled;
translations.idiomatic: You Ziyuan’s counsel briefly stilled the war banners;

sentences.zh: 和苞獻直，酆明罷觀。

translations.literal: He Bao offered bluntness—the Fengming observatory was halted.
translations.idiomatic: He Bao’s remonstrance stopped the Fengming tower.

sentences.zh: 而師之所處，荊棘生焉，自絕強籓，禍成勁敵。

translations.literal: But where armies march, brambles grow; cutting off a strong vassal, disaster became a stalwart foe.
translations.idiomatic: Yet armies leave thorns; severing a mighty vassal bred a deadly enemy.

sentences.zh: 天之所厭，人事以之，駭戰士而宵奔，酌戎杯而不醒，有若假手，同乎拾芥。

translations.literal: What heaven detested, men completed—soldiers bolted by night, he drained barbarian cups yet never sobered; as if heaven lent a hand, easy as picking up mustard.
translations.idiomatic: Heaven’s curse and human folly met: troops fled by night while he drowned in drink—he fell as if heaven struck, swift as snatching weed-seed.

sentences.zh: 豈石氏之興歟，何不支之甚也！

translations.literal: Was it the Shi clan’s rise? How utterly he could not endure!
translations.idiomatic: Was it merely Shi’s fortune? No—his collapse was utter.

sentences.zh: 贊曰：惟皇不範，邇甸居穹。

translations.literal: Encomium: The sovereign spurned the model; the near fields housed the dome.
translations.idiomatic: Encomium: The true king’s pattern was cast aside; barbarians camped on the heartland.

sentences.zh: 丹硃罕嗣，冒頓爭雄。

translations.literal: Dan Zhu rarely succeeded; Modun strove for supremacy.
translations.idiomatic: Dan Zhu won no throne; Modun seized hegemony.

sentences.zh: 胡旌揚月，朔馬騰風。

translations.literal: Hu banners lifted the moon; northern horses rode the wind.
translations.idiomatic: Hu flags brushed the moon; steppe horses rode the gale.

sentences.zh: 埃塵淮浦，虓呼河宮。

translations.literal: Dust veiled the Huai’s shore; tiger-shouts shook the river halls.
translations.idiomatic: Dust cloaked Huai’s banks; tiger-cries rocked the river palaces.

sentences.zh: 未央朝寂，謻門旦空。

translations.literal: Weiyang’s dawn was still; Yimen’s morning stood empty.
translations.idiomatic: Weiyang fell silent at dawn; Yimen stood empty by daybreak.

sentences.zh: 郭欽之慮，辛有知戎。

translations.literal: Guo Qin’s warning—Xin You knew the Rong.
translations.idiomatic: Guo Qin foretold the peril; Xin You knew the barbarians would come.
